Do ahead: Soup can be made 3 days ahead; refrigerate in an airtight container or freeze for up to 6 months. Reheat over medium until steaming.

To serve, position a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat the broiler to high. Cut two 1/2-inch baguette slices for every serving of soup. Place baguette slices on a rimmed baking sheet and toast in oven until crisp and dry but not browned, about 1 minute per side. Rub one side of each toast with the 1 garlic clove, cut in half lengthwise, and set aside.

Place ramekins, crocks, or ovensafe bowls on a rimmed baking sheet, add 1/2 tsp. sherry, preferably Fino or Manzanilla, to the bottom of each, and ladle soup on top. Top each serving of soup with two garlic-rubbed toasts. Divide 4 oz. (about 1 cup) coarsely grated Gruyère cheese among the servings, covering the toasted bread slices and some of the soup. Carefully transfer baking sheet to oven and broil until cheese is melted and bubbling, 4–8 minutes. (Alternatively, if using regular soup bowls: Top each garlic-rubbed toast with some cheese and return to broiler to melt, about 2 minutes more. Divide sherry and soup among bowls, sprinkle with remaining cheese, and top each serving with two cheese toasts.)

cultural relevance.reasoning: Onion-based broths date back to ancient Roman and medieval peasant times because onions were cheap and plentiful.

title: Pani Puri
description: Pani puri is a popular Indian street food of crispy, fried, hollow dough balls that are stuffed with boiled potatoes, steamed moong sprouts, spicy tangy water and sweet chutney.

ingredients.raw: black salt or regular salt or pink salt, as required (stuffing)
1/2 cup chopped mint leaves – tightly packed (pani)
1 cup chopped coriander leaves – tightly packed (cilantro) (pani)
2 to 3 green chilies – chopped (for a less spicy pani, add about 1 green chili) (pani)
3.5 to 4 tablespoons jaggery powder or grated/chopped jaggery or sugar, add as required (pani)
1 to 1.25 cups water to be added later, add water as per the consistency you want (pani)
1 to 1.5 tablespoons boondi (fried tiny gram flour balls), optional (pani)
black salt or regular salt, add as required (pani)
24 to 30 puris you could buy these puris readymade or make them at home
1 small bowl Tamarind Chutney or tamarind dates chutney – optional

steps: Making pani puri stuffing: Boil the potatoes till they are cooked completely.
Peel them and then chop them.
Finely chop the onion if using it.
In a small bowl, mix the potatoes, onions, coriander leaves, cumin powder, chaat masala powder and black salt or regular salt. Mix well and keep aside.
Making pani (spiced water): In a blender add all the ingredients mentioned above for the pani.
Add water and grind to a fine chutney.
Remove the green chutney in a large bowl. Rinse the mixer jar with 1/2 cup water first and then add this water in the bowl. Then add 1/2 to 3/4 cup more water.

Mix well. Check the seasoning. Add more salt or jeera powder or chaat masala or jaggery if required. If you want a thin pani, you could add some water. But keep on checking the seasoning, as per your taste.
Add the boondi to the pani.
You can chill the pani in the fridge or add some ice cubes to it.
Assembling pani puri: Crack the top of the puri with a spoon.
Add 2 to 3 teaspoons of the boiled potato-onion filling in the poori.
Stir the green pani first and then add it in the poori. Optionally you can add some sweet chutney in the puri.
Serve the pani puri immediately otherwise the prepared puri with stuffing and water will become soggy.
You can also make individual portions with the puris, potato-onion mixture and the pani. Let the individual assemble the pani puri for himself/herself as per his/her taste.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It is an iconic social street food that brings people together around roadside stalls. Eating it is an interactive, communal experience where vendors assemble each piece fresh for the customer to eat in a single bite.

title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Muffins

ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup coarsely chopped raw pumpkin seeds (streusel)
1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt (filling)
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled (batter)
1 Tbsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract (batter)
1 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt (batter)
Vegetable oil or nonstick vegetable oil spray (for ice cream scoop)

steps: Streusel: Whisk 1/3 cup coarsely chopped raw pumpkin seeds, 1/4 cup (31 g) all-purpose flour, 2 Tbsp. light brown sugar, 1/2 tsp. pumpkin pie spice, and a pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl to combine. Using your fingers, rub in 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, until moist pea-size lumps form. Chill until ready to use.

Filling: Vigorously whisk 6 oz. cream cheese, room temperature, 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, 2 tsp. all-purpose flour, 2 tsp. vanilla extract, and 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl until combined and smooth.

Batter and assembly: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 375°. Line cups of a standard 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners. Whisk 2 large eggs, 1 1/2 cups (packed; 300 g) light brown sugar, 1 cup canned pumpkin purée, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, 1/4 cup whole milk, 1 Tbsp. pumpkin pie spice, 1 Tbsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, and 1 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth, about 1 minute. Whisk 1 3/4 cups (219 g) all-purpose flour and 1 1/2 tsp. baking powder in a small bowl to combine. Add to pumpkin mixture and fold in with a rubber spatula until just incorporated and no large dry streaks of flour remain (don't overmix; batter will be lumpy).

Lightly coat the inside of a #12 cookie scoop or 1/3-cup measuring cup with vegetable oil or nonstick vegetable oil spray and evenly divide batter among muffin cups (they will be full). Transfer filling to a piping bag (or a resealable plastic bag with 1 corner snipped off). Working one at a time and dividing evenly, insert bag about halfway into batter and pipe in some filling, ending with a swirl on top of batter. Top each muffin with some streusel, gently pressing to adhere (use all of it).

Bake muffins until streusel is crisp and muffins spring back when gently pressed, 24–27 minutes. Let muffins cool in pan 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and let cool until just warm or completely.
Do Ahead: Muffins can be made 2 days ahead. Store airtight at room temperature.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Modern Americal fall staple popularized by Starbucks.

title: The Best Homemade New York Bagels
description: Chewy New York style bagels fresh from your own oven.

ingredients.raw: 1/2 Tbsp (4g) minced dried garlic (everything bagel seasoning)
2.5 tsp (18g) barley malt syrup, or 1 Tbsp (13g) granulated sugar
1/2 red onion, very thinly sliced (to serve)
2 large tomatoes, very thinly sliced (to serve)
1 bunch fresh dill, fronds picked (to serve)

steps: Everything bagel seasoning: Combine the sesame seeds, poppy seeds, onion, garlic, and flaky salt in a small bowl and toss to combine.

Bagels: In a medium sized bowl, add your water then whisk in the yeast and barley malt syrup until dissolved. In a separate large bowl, whisk your bread flour and fine sea salt until combined. Pour the wet into the dry and mix together with your hand until you get a rough but cohesive dough, with no dry bits remaining. If it is too dry, add 1 tablespoon of water, knead, and repeat as necessary until it comes together as a uniform dough.

Turn out onto a counter and knead for 3-5 minutes or until the dough is completely smooth and passes the windowpane test. To check for gluten development using the windowpane test, pinch and pull a small section of dough. If you can see light through the stretched dough without it tearing, you can stop kneading. Alternatively, you could do all this in a stand mixer if you prefer. Return the dough to a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rest for 30-45 minutes at room temperature. It's okay if the dough doesn't quite double fully in size.

Divide the dough into 8 pieces, each weighing about 128g each. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray and then evenly sprinkle with a thin coating of fine cornmeal. There are 3 shaping techniques that you can use. Hand Roll Method: Roll out a piece of your dough into an even 7" log. Grab one side with the palm of your hand then wrap the other end around your knuckles to meet the 2nd end. Press the ends together then roll and press that seam until fully adhered. Montreal Style: Roll out a piece of your dough into an even 8" log. Flatten one end with a rolling pin then take the other side and coil it to lay the 2nd end in the middle of the flattened edge. Pull the edges of the flattened part around the log to enclose the 2nd end. Press and pinch the seam together until fully closed. The Easy Method (although untraditional): Shape each of those pieces into a ball by rolling it on the countertop in a circular motion, using slight pressure and keeping the dough in constant contact with the work surface. Cover the balls with a damp towel or plastic wrap and let them rest for 10-15 minutes. Press a hole in the center of the ball using your thumb and index finger, then stretch the hole while rotating the bagel so it's stretched evenly, to your desired size and shape.

Place the shaped bagels on the prepared baking sheet. Lightly spray the tops of the bagels with cooking spray and then cover the baking sheet tightly with greased plastic wrap. Make it as airtight as you can without squishing the bagels. Leave out at room temperature for 5-10 minutes to kickstart the fermentation process, then place in the refrigerator to proof overnight.
When the proofing time is complete, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper sprayed with cooking spray.

To a 6-7 quart (5.7-6.6 L) pot, add the water, salt, barley malt syrup, and optionally lye (being careful not to splash any on you). Whisk until combined. Place over medium-high heat, and bring to a boil. Wearing food-safe gloves, gently lay in the bagels top-side down to the water, working in batches to avoid overcrowding. Boil for 30 seconds, flip, and cook for another 30 seconds. Using a spider or slotted spoon, drain and transfer the bagels to your prepared baking sheet, four bagels per tray.
Immediately sprinkle your bagels generously with your everything bagel seasoning if using so it sticks to the still-tacky surface of the bagels.

Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until they turn a rich golden brown on the exterior. Transfer the bagels to a wire rack to cool completely. These are best enjoyed the same day they're baked, but you can keep your leftovers in an airtight container or plastic bag for up to 4-5 days. Toast them to bring them back to life. If you want to keep them longer, freeze them.

To serve: Slice your bagel in half then schmear both sides with your whipped cream cheese. Season your tomato slice with flaky salt and place on the bottom slice. Top that with nova lox, red onion, dill, and capers. Crown your king then serve and enjoy!

Notes: The addition of food grade lye is something that's done very commonly to make traditional pretzels. If you are going to use it, please make sure that you are using gloves and avoid allowing the mixture to touch your skin. The addition of lye is completely safe to eat after the bagels are baked, it just helps the bagels obtain a little extra crisp and burnished browning on the exterior. If you don't have lye and don't want to buy it you could substitute a teaspoon of baking soda. It won't be as dramatic but it will help a little with making an alkaline solution.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It is an enduring symbol of New York City food culture, famous for traditional pairings like cream cheese, lox, capers, and deli meats.

title: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes)
description: A quick, one-pan Turkish dish of soft scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes, peppers, and onions.

ingredients.raw: 1 green bell pepper (Anaheim or Holland peppers will work as well), cored, seeded and chopped
1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper, more for later
Crushed red pepper flakes, optional if you like spicy
1 French baguette for serving thickly sliced (optional)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper with a pinch of salt and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft but not browned.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste. Season with more salt, black pepper, oregano, and Aleppo pepper. Cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften but keep their shape.
Push the vegetables to one side and lower the heat to medium-low. Add the beaten eggs and cook gently, stirring as needed, until just set. Fold the vegetables into the eggs.
Drizzle with a little olive oil, add more Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes if desired, and serve immediately with thick slices of bread.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Menemen is a defining element of the traditional Turkish breakfast.

title: The Best Hamantaschen Recipe Ever
description: A sugar-cookie-style hamantaschen dough, rolled, filled, and baked into triangular Purim cookies.

ingredients.raw: 1 stick (1/2 cup) unsalted butter or margarine, at room temperature
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
filling of choice (about 1/2 tsp per cookie)

steps: Beat the butter and sugar until smooth.
Mix in the egg, milk, vanilla, and lemon zest.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add the dry mixture to the wet until combined. If the dough is too soft, add flour a few tablespoons at a time until it firms up.
Form the dough into a disk, wrap it, and chill for at least 1 hour (up to 24 hours).
Dust the work surface with flour and roll the dough to about 1/4 inch thick.
Cut out 3-inch rounds and place them on a cookie sheet, dipping the cutter in flour before each cut.
Place 1/2 tsp of filling in the center of each round and pinch the corners together tightly to form triangles.
Chill the shaped cookies for 10 minutes in the fridge or 5 minutes in the freezer so they hold their shape.
Bake at 400°F for 7 to 9 minutes.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Ashkenazi Jewish communities adopted these sweet poppy-seed pockets, renaming them hamantaschen.

title: Classic Loco Moco
description: A simple home version of the Hilo-born local favorite: a burger and fried egg over rice, smothered in mushroom gravy.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups Waimea Butcher Shop beef bone broth
4 6 oz. Lewis Cattle Co. beef burgers
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Sauté the quartered mushrooms in olive oil over high heat in a medium saucepan, then season with salt and pepper.
Once the mushrooms are fully cooked, add the beef broth and bring to a simmer.
Whisk the cornstarch and cold water into a slurry, stir it into the broth, and keep whisking until the gravy thickens. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Heat a cast iron pan over medium-high heat. Season the burgers with salt and pepper, then cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until done to your liking.
In a small nonstick pan over medium heat with a little oil, crack in an egg, add 1 teaspoon of water, and cover until fully cooked. Season with salt and pepper.
Place a scoop of rice on a plate, top with a burger, smother with mushroom gravy, add the egg, and garnish with micro greens.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It evolved from a cheap 30-cent after-school diner special for kids into a cornerstone of Hawaiian plate lunch culture, served everywhere from roadside shacks and local diners to high-end resort menus.

title: Tuna Noodle Casserole (From Scratch!)
description: A from-scratch casserole with a cheesy homemade sauce, marinated tuna, vegetables, peas, and a potato chip and bread crumb topping.

ingredients.raw: 1/2 ounce (14.17 g) Monterey Jack cheese, shredded (topping)
1/2 ounce (14.17 g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded (topping)
2 slices white sandwich bread, torn into 1-inch pieces (topping)
3 (140g) 5-ounce cans solid white albacore tuna packed in water
10 ounces (283.5 g) white mushrooms, sliced 1/4-inch thick
1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded, and finely chopped
3 1/2 ounces (99.22 g) Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
3 1/2 ounces (99.22 g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the two topping cheeses in a bowl. Pulse the chips, bread, 1/4 cup of the cheese mix, 2 tablespoons butter, and 1/4 teaspoon each of salt and pepper in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Set aside.

Press the tuna dry in a fine-mesh strainer with paper towels, then flake it in a large bowl. Microwave the oil, lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper for about 30 seconds, stir into the tuna, and set aside.
Boil 4 quarts of water in a Dutch oven. Cook the noodles with 1 tablespoon salt until al dente, drain, rinse with cold water for about 2 minutes, drain again, and set aside.
In the empty pot, melt 1 tablespoon butter over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms with 1/4 teaspoon salt until the liquid evaporates and they brown, 6 to 8 minutes. Move them to the tuna bowl.
Melt another tablespoon of butter in the pot. Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened, about 5 minutes. Add them to the tuna and mushroom mixture.

Melt the last 2 tablespoons of butter in the pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour until golden, about 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the half-and-half and broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer 5 to 7 minutes until slightly thickened.
Off the heat, whisk in the shredded cheese until smooth. Stir in the noodles, the tuna-vegetable mixture, the peas, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon each of salt and pepper.
Spread everything in a 9x13-inch baking dish, top with the crumb mixture, and bake 12 to 14 minutes until golden brown.
Let the casserole rest on a wire rack for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Galette des Rois with Frangipane
description: A classic French King's Cake for the Epiphany, with an almond frangipane filling sealed inside flaky puff pastry.

ingredients.raw: 125 g (1 stick plus 1 tablespoon) unsalted butter, softened (frangipane)
1 teaspoon rum, or vanilla extract, optional (frangipane)
2 sheets puff pastry, preferably made from butter
1 porcelain fève, large dried bean or large coin wrapped in foil

steps: Cream the butter and sugar in a stand mixer with the paddle until pale yellow. Beat in the egg, egg yolk, and rum or vanilla if using.
Add the ground almonds, flour, and salt and mix until fully incorporated. Chill the frangipane for about 30 to 60 minutes.
For the egg wash, lightly whisk the egg yolk and milk together.
Place one puff pastry sheet on a large piece of baking paper and cut a circle about 23 to 26 cm across, using a plate or cake tin as a guide. Prick it lightly with a fork, leaving a 2 cm border.
Spread the frangipane evenly inside the border and hide the fève in the filling near the edge. Brush the border with egg wash.
Cut the second sheet of pastry to the same size, lay it over the filling, and press and seal the edges.
Chill the galette for about 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180°C / 350°F (no fan) with a metal baking tray inside.
Brush the top with egg wash and, if you like, score a decorative pattern without cutting all the way through.
Slide the galette on its baking paper onto the hot tray and bake for about 35 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Serve at room temperature. Whoever finds the fève in their slice is crowned King or Queen.

cultural relevance.reasoning: The tradition dates back to the 13th or 14th century in France, evolving from ancient Roman Saturnalia winter solstice festivals.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
description: A one-pan, oven-baked take on chicken fajitas with seasoned chicken, roasted bell peppers and onions, and lime, served in tortillas.

ingredients.raw: 2 small/medium boneless, skinless chicken breasts, lightly pounded to even thickness (about 1 1/4 lb total)
2 large bell peppers (red, yellow, green, or orange), seeded and cut into 1/2-inch strips
1 red onion, halved and cut into 1/2-inch strips
Sour cream or plain Greek yogurt (for serving)

steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Pound the chicken breasts to an even thickness of about 1/2 to 3/4 inch.
Place the sliced peppers and onion on one side of a baking sheet and the chicken on the other. Squeeze one lime over the chicken and the other over the vegetables.
Drizzle the vegetables with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and the chicken with the rest.
Mix the chili powder, garlic powder, cumin, salt, onion powder, and cayenne (if using). Sprinkle over the chicken and vegetables and toss to coat, rubbing the chicken on both sides.
If the pan is crowded, move about two-thirds of the vegetables to a second sheet pan.
Roast 15 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F, tossing the vegetables once halfway through. During the last 5 minutes, wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven.
Let the chicken rest briefly, then slice thinly. Fill the tortillas with chicken, vegetables, cilantro, and toppings.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Inspired in Mexican beef fajitas, this is a staple of Texan food.

title: Cachapas with Poblano Sauce

ingredients.raw: Seasoning powder (optional, for more flavor) (poblano sauce)
Queso de mano or a substitute (cachapa)

steps: Poblano sauce: Char the poblano chiles directly over a flame or under the broiler until blackened all over. Place them in a covered bowl for about 10 minutes, then peel, seed, and devein them.
Blend the roasted poblanos with the cottage cheese, table cream, salt, garlic powder, and seasoning powder (if using) until smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Cachapa batter: Blend the drained corn, Harina PAN, eggs, cottage cheese, a pinch of salt, and sugar to taste until you have a thick, slightly chunky batter. Let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and melt a little butter. Pour in about 1/3 cup of batter and spread it into a round about 5 to 6 inches across.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, 3 to 4 minutes, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until golden. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter as needed.
Place a slice of queso de mano on each hot cachapa, fold it in half, and serve with the poblano sauce.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Cachapas are a cornerstone of Venezuelan identity and culinary heritage. This is a fusion recipe with poblano sauce, originating from the Puebla region in Mexico.

title: Batch Carajillo
steps: Once you mix everything together pop it in fridge.
Fill your shaker with ice and half way with the carajillo mix and shake vigorously for like 10 seconds. Pour over fresh ice.
Or you can fill the pitcher with ice, give it a good stir, and let it sit for 5ish min, to help it dilute some more if you would prefer not shake.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Most populat legend traces the drink to Spanish colonial troops in Cuba. Soliders mixed coffee and alcohol"for courage" before going into battle.

title: Atún Toreado (Tuna with Blistered Chile)
steps: Brown the onion and chile in olive oil, then combine with the tuna, the cucumber chopped into small pieces, and the olives.
For the dressing: mix the soy sauce, two tablespoons of olive oil, rice vinegar, lime juice, cilantro, and garlic powder. Salt and pepper to taste.
Mix both together and it's ready.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Modern Mexican dish. Historically canned tuna was the primary way this fish was consumed in central Mexico because of its affordabllity. Adding the "toreado" chilies elevated the dish into a contemporary Mexican gastronomy centerpice.

title: Tuna Tiradito (Tiradito de Atún)
steps: Arrange slices of tuna steak alternating with slices of avocado on a shallow bowl-style plate.
Separately, for the dressing, mix: lime juice, sesame oil, salt, garlic powder, sriracha, chives, and Maggi seasoning sauce.
Garnish with cilantro, sesame seeds, red onion, mango, and very thinly sliced cucumber.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Japanese immigration to Peru began in 1899. A large Japanese community settled along the Peruvian coast and imigrants opened cevicherias and restaurants in Lima, where they blended their knife skills with local ingradients.

title: Red Rice (Arroz Rojo)
steps: Brown the rice to seal each grain so it doesn't stick.
Prepare the recaudo with tomato, onion, cumin, and garlic (blend).
Add the recaudo to the rice, making sure to drain the extra oil before adding it. Let the recaudo brown.
Rinse the blender with water and add double the amount of water to the rice (boiling).
Add half a jalapeño chile before covering (to add flavor). Simmer over low heat for 17 minutes. Uncover and stir carefully to fluff the rice. Cover again and let rest for 5-7 minutes before serving.

cultural relevance.reasoning: One of the most common side dishes in Mexican cuisine. It is celebratory dish that symbolizes the historical blending of Indigenous, Spanish, and African culinary traditions.

title: Arepas Reina Pepiada

ingredients.raw: Harina P.A.N (or other precooked corn flour) - 200g (arepas)

steps: Poaching liquid: Add the stock, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, parsley, MSG, lime peel and salt to a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes to infuse. Taste; it should be salty, aromatic and strong. Adjust if needed and make sure there's enough liquid to cover the chicken.

Chicken: Add the chicken breasts and lower the heat to 80-90°C (180-200°F), hot but not boiling. Keep within this range and poach until cooked, around 20 minutes depending on breast size. Don't worry if it boils occasionally; it won't ruin anything, lower temperatures just yield softer chicken. Once cooked, remove, rest, cool and shred.

Filling: Dice the onion, finely chop the coriander and open the avocado. Smash the avocado with a mortar and pestle or fork, then add the chicken, onion, coriander, lime juice and mayo. Season with salt, cover and refrigerate.
Dough: Dissolve the salt in the water in a large bowl. Add the corn flour and mix until a ball forms. Cover and rest for 10 minutes to fully hydrate, then divide into 4 balls.

Fry: Heat a frying pan on medium-low with a thin layer of neutral oil. Flatten each dough ball into a circle about 1 cm thick and add to the pan. Don't rush; the centres need time to cook. Flip every couple of minutes, slowly building a light golden brown exterior, around 12-15 minutes total. Set aside to cool until you can handle them.
Assemble: Using a butter knife, cut into each arepa. The inside should be tacky but fully cooked, not wet and sloppy. Stuff with the Reina Pepiada filling and optionally serve with hot sauce.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Famous Venezuelan arepa dedicated to 1950s Susana Duijm, Venezuela's first Miss World.

title: Pasta with Tuna in the Style of Puttanesca

ingredients.raw: Chilli flakes - 1/2 tsp (or more if you like it spicy)
Olive oil (pantry; the method uses around 2 to 3 tbsp)

steps: Prep: Thinly slice the garlic, pit and roughly chop the olives, chop the parsley, and halve the tomatoes.

Base: Heat a frying pan on medium-low and add enough olive oil to coat the bottom (around 2 to 3 tbsp). Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute. Add the anchovies, capers and tomatoes. Season with salt and cook for a few minutes until the tomatoes start to blister. Keep it stirring and moving.
Pasta: Prepare your pasta as per the packet instructions in salty boiling water. Cook it slightly under al dente, as you will finish the pasta in the pan with the sauce.

Bring it together: Back in the pan, keep the base cooking and the tomatoes breaking down. Prepare your tin of tuna. Once the pasta is just under al dente, add it to the pan, reserving the pasta water. Mix everything together, adding pasta water to create and loosen the sauce. Add the tuna to the pan, mix it gently to preserve some larger chunks, then add half of your parsley and combine. Once the pasta is cooked al dente it's ready; taste for seasoning and adjust.
Plating: Get the pasta onto a plate and top with the remaining parsley. Good alternative toppings include toasted breadcrumbs, some kind of hard cheese, black pepper, etc. Enjoy immediately!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Puttanesca originates from the Campania region in South Italy. While this is not the traditional recipe, it's an affordable interpretation.

title: Chicken, Delicata Squash
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F.

Clean your delicata squash, cut it in half lengthwise, scoop out the seeds, and cut it crosswise into 1 cm strips. Prep your Brussels sprouts and onions, then add all the vegetables to a baking sheet.
Drizzle with a good glug of olive oil, add a generous pinch of salt and pepper, and toss in 2-3 sprigs each of fresh rosemary and thyme. Mix everything together with your hands and roast in the oven.
Pat your chicken thighs dry and heavily season the skin side with salt and pepper. Place them skin side down in a cold cast-iron or stainless steel pan, then turn the heat to medium.
Season the flesh side with your favorite rub or simply salt and pepper. Cook for about 15 minutes, or until the skin is deeply golden and releases easily from the pan.

Remove the vegetables from the oven and nestle the chicken thighs on top, skin side up. Return the baking sheet to the oven and roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are tender.
While everything finishes roasting, make your pan sauce in the same pan you cooked the chicken in. Add your minced shallot and garlic with a pinch of salt. Cook over low heat for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in your chicken stock, increase the heat to medium, and reduce by about half. Add your heavy cream and continue reducing until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Turn off the heat and strain out the shallot and garlic.
Whisk in your Dijon and whole-grain mustard, taste, and adjust the salt as needed.
Plate the roasted vegetables, top with a chicken thigh or two, and sauce.
Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Piccata inspired, this is an Italian-American interpretation with fall ingredients (delicata squash.

title: Vodka Sauce for Pasta

ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup 'nduja, more if you want extra spicy

steps: Chop the onion and slice the garlic. Add them to the pan with olive oil.
Add the 'nduja and let it cook.
Add the vodka and let the alcohol evaporate, a couple of minutes, then add the crushed tomatoes and simmer gently for 20-30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in the mascarpone at the end, before serving.
Finish with some shaved parmigiana and freshly cracked black pepper.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Adding vodka to a tomato sauce first happened in Rome in the 1970 as part of a vodka promotional campaging with actor Ugo Tognazzi.

title: Red Curry, Bone Broth and Coconut Bowl

ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp Fit Me beef tallow (for the meat)
1 tsp freshly grated ginger (for the meat)
1 tbsp Fit Me beef tallow (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 garlic clove, finely chopped (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tsp freshly grated ginger (for the coconut red curry broth)
2 tbsp Thai red curry paste (for the coconut red curry broth)
3 cups Fit Me beef bone broth (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 can (400 ml / 13.5 oz) coconut milk (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tbsp soy sauce (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tsp fish sauce (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tsp hoisin sauce (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tsp rice vinegar (for the coconut red curry broth)
1-2 tsp lime juice (for the coconut red curry broth)
1 tsp sesame oil (for the coconut red curry broth)

steps: Crispy beef: Heat a wide pot over medium-high heat with the beef tallow. Add the ground beef and fry until it browns.
Remove the beef and set it aside.
Coconut red curry broth: In the same pot, add the second tablespoon of beef tallow, then the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds. Add the white part of the green onion.
Stir in the red curry paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring to release its aromas.
Add the Fit Me beef bone broth, the coconut milk, the soy sauce, the fish sauce, the hoisin sauce and the rice vinegar.
Bring to a gentle boil and cook for 3-5 minutes. Remove from the heat and add the lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Plating: Place a generous portion of jasmine rice in each bowl.
Serve the hot coconut red curry broth around the rice.
Add the crispy beef on one side and arrange the fresh cucumber.
Finish with the sesame oil, cilantro, green onion, Thai basil, black sesame seeds and lime to taste.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Thai Red Curry originated in central Thailand. This recipe mixes the traditional red curry with bone broth to improve gut-health.

title: Roast Chicken, Mashed Potatoes, Gravy, Vegetables

ingredients.raw: 3-4 Yukon Gold Potatoes, cut into 1 inch pieces (roasted veggies)

steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F.

Spatchcock your chicken by using a pair of kitchen shears to remove the backbone. Drizzle the chicken with a little olive oil, then generously season both sides with salt and the skin with black pepper.
Prepare your vegetables and add them to a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Place a wire rack over the vegetables, then place the chicken on top.
Roast the chicken for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until the thickest part of the breast reaches 155°F.

While the chicken is cooking, make your gravy. Add butter to a saucepan over medium-low heat. Once melted, add plenty of black pepper, followed by the shallot and garlic. Add a pinch of salt and slowly sauté for about 5-6 minutes, or until softened.
Add the flour and turn the heat up to medium. Stir and cook for about 2-3 minutes to make your roux and cook off the raw flour.
Slowly pour in the chicken stock while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer, then add the rosemary and thyme. Continue simmering for about 10 minutes, or until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the gravy from the heat. It will thicken a little more as it cools.
Once the chicken is done, let it rest for 10-15 minutes before carving.
Serve the chicken with the roasted vegetables and plenty of gravy.
Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Core part of the traditional Sunday roast meal that dates back to medieval England.

title: Pumpkin Chai Latte Loaf

ingredients.raw: 468 g pumpkin purée - your entire 16.5 oz can (wet ingredients)
100 g packed brown sugar - 1/2 cup (wet ingredients)
75 g granulated sugar - about 1/3 cup + 1 Tbsp (wet ingredients)
100 g pure maple syrup - about 1/4 cup + 1 Tbsp (wet ingredients)
120 g full-fat Greek yogurt - 1/2 cup (wet ingredients)
120 g unsalted butter, melted and cooled - about 1/2 cup + 1 Tbsp (wet ingredients)
3 tablespoons of cinnamon (split the batter then add)
1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice (split the batter then add)
1 extra teaspoon vanilla bean paste (split the batter then add)
1/2 cup loose chai tea leaves (split the batter then add)
8oz cream cheese (vanilla bean cream cheese frosting)
2 cups powdered sugar (vanilla bean cream cheese frosting)
2 teaspoon vanilla bean paste (vanilla bean cream cheese frosting)
Pinch salt (vanilla bean cream cheese frosting)
Sprinkle of cinnamon on top (vanilla bean cream cheese frosting)

steps: Prepare: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and line it with parchment, leaving some overhang.
Combine the dry ingredients: Whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and pumpkin pie spice.
Melt the butter: Melt the 120 g butter and let it cool until warm, not hot.

Mix the wet ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the melted butter, brown sugar, granulated sugar, and maple syrup. Whisk in the eggs, one at a time. Add the pumpkin purée, Greek yogurt, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth.
Combine: Add the dry ingredients to the pumpkin mixture. Fold gently just until the flour disappears. Do not overmix.
Split the batter: Divide the batter in half. Stir the 3 tablespoons of cinnamon, 1 tablespoon of pumpkin pie spice, the extra teaspoon of vanilla bean paste and the chai tea leaves into one half.

Bake: Transfer both batters to the prepared 9x5-inch loaf pan. Bake at 350°F for approximately 65-75 minutes. Start checking around 60-65 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out with a few moist crumbs, but no wet batter. If the top becomes deeply browned before the center is finished, loosely tent it with foil.
Cool: Let the loaf cool in the pan for 15-20 minutes, then lift it out onto a cooling rack.
Frost (highly recommended, because the loaf itself is not very sweet): Combine the frosting ingredients in your stand mixer. Spread over the loaf and sprinkle with cinnamon.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Modern Americal fall staple. It combines elements of Indian spiced chai tea.

title: High-Protein Basque Cheesecake (Cottage Cheese Edition)
description: Burnt, creamy, jiggly... Macros per slice (15 slices): 220-260 kcal, 18-20 g protein, 15-18 g carbs, 11-13 g fat.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese until smooth, then blend it with the cream cheese.
Mix in the eggs, vanilla, salt, cornstarch and honey.
Bake Basque style at 200°C for 45-55 minutes, until the top is dark and burnt and the center still jiggles.
Chill for a minimum of 4 hours.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Basque cheescake originated in San Sebastian, in Spain's Basque Country. This presentation has a higher protein content because of the cottage cheese.

title: Shio Koji Marinated Whole Chicken with White Miso Beurre Blanc and Burnt Leek Ash Oil
description: A whole butterflied chicken, marinated overnight in shio koji, roasted until beautifully golden, and served over a miso beurre blanc with leek ash oil. It's genuinely one of the BEST of the BEST chickens you'll ever make: exceptionally tender, juicy and packed with umami. Shio koji is, after all, one of Japan's secrets to incredibly juicy, flavourful meat.

ingredients.raw: 1 whole chicken, approx. 2kg, butterflied (for the chicken)
Shio koji, enough to coat the chicken generously (for the chicken)
250g unsalted butter, cold and cubed (for the miso beurre blanc)
200ml dry white wine (for the miso beurre blanc)
60ml rice vinegar (for the miso beurre blanc)
2 large shallot, finely chopped (for the miso beurre blanc)
2.5 tbsp white miso (for the miso beurre blanc)
3 tbsp double cream (optional) (for the miso beurre blanc)
Green leek tops (for the leek ash oil)
Neutral oil (for the leek ash oil)

steps: Chicken: Coat the butterflied chicken generously with shio koji and leave to marinate in the fridge overnight (mine was marinated for around 18 hours).
Remove any heavy excess marinade from the surface before cooking.
Place the chicken into the air fryer skin side up.
Cook on Steam + Air Fry at 160°C for 25 minutes, then finish on Air Fry at 180°C for 10 minutes until golden and completely cooked through.
Allow the chicken to rest before serving.
Miso beurre blanc: Add the finely chopped shallot, white wine and rice vinegar to a small saucepan.
Simmer until the liquid has reduced considerably and you're left with just a small amount of liquid.
Turn the heat down very low and gradually whisk in the cold butter, a few cubes at a time, allowing each addition to emulsify before adding more.
Add the double cream.
Once smooth and glossy, whisk in the white miso. Strain the sauce for a velvety finish.
Keep the sauce warm over very gentle heat; don't allow it to boil.
Leek ash oil: Roast the green leek tops until completely blackened and crisp.
Allow them to cool, then blitz or crush them into a fine ash.
Combine with neutral oil and blend until you have a deep black leek oil.
Strain the oil using a muslin cloth.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Fusion of Japanese ingredients (miso) and French techniques (beurre blanc).

title: Chocolate Pot de Crème
description: Rich, creamy, crunchy, warm and spiced.

ingredients.raw: 4 1/2 oz high-quality semisweet chocolate, chopped (I use a single origin Italian chocolate you can get from Eataly)

steps: Add the chopped chocolate to a glass bowl.

Warm the milk and 1/2 cup of the heavy cream in a saucepan with the saffron, crushed cardamom pods, cinnamon stick and clove, let the spices steep, then remove them. Whisk in the egg yolks, sugar and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of a spatula and is just shy of boiling, about 5-6 minutes.
Immediately pour the hot custard over the chocolate and hand-blend until completely smooth.
Pour into ramekins, glasses or a sealed container and refrigerate until set, about 2 hours.
Whip the remaining 1/4 cup heavy cream to soft peaks. I leave mine unsweetened; the chocolate and candied walnuts bring plenty of sweetness.
Chai-spiced candied walnuts: Melt the sugar to a caramel color and candy the walnuts in it until glossy and toasted. Season generously with the spices and salt, then spread out to cool completely.
Finish each pot de crème with a spoonful of whipped cream, crushed spiced walnuts and a light dusting of chai.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Classic baked custard dessert that originated in France in the 17th century.

title: Steak Frites with Bone Marrow Bordelaise
description: A classic.

ingredients.raw: Steak of choice (1-1 1/4 lb) 1-1 1/2 inches thick (Wagyu Zabuton used here; ribeye, NY strip, and hanger are all great choices) (for the steak)
Kosher salt (3/4 tsp) per pound (for the steak)
Neutral oil for searing (for the steak)
Shallot (1 medium, finely minced) (for the bordelaise)
Garlic (2 cloves, finely minced) (for the bordelaise)
Dry red wine (2 cups) or Bordeaux, Cabernet, or Côtes du Rhône (for the bordelaise)
Bone marrow (1/4 cup, scooped from the bones) match the amount of butter you'd otherwise finish the sauce with, since the marrow is doing that job here (for the bordelaise)
Neutral oil (2-3 Tbsp) enough to coat generously (for the frites)

steps: The night before: Submerge the bone marrow pieces (1/4 cup) (if using) in a bowl of cold water with a generous pinch of salt. Refrigerate overnight. This pulls out any blood and impurities and leaves you with clean, neutral fat.

Season the steak (1-1 1/4 lb) with kosher salt (3/4 tsp) per pound. Place uncovered on a rack in the fridge. The dry brine will draw out moisture, then reabsorb it; you'll get better seasoning and a drier surface for searing. This step is optional, and if you choose to skip it, season your steak right before searing.
Before you cook: Pull the steak from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking to take the chill off the center. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Remove the bone marrow from its brine and pat completely dry. Scoop the marrow out of the bones; you want about 1/4 cup total for the sauce.

Frites (start first), oven method: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a sheet tray with parchment paper. Toss the frozen frites with enough neutral oil (2-3 Tbsp) to coat generously and spread in an even layer. Roast for 20-30 minutes, tossing every 10 minutes so they cook evenly. Salt aggressively the moment they come out. Start the frites before anything else happens with the steak; they need to be ready at the same time as everything else. If they finish early, you can always re-crisp/reheat them in the oven for 2-3 minutes right before plating.

Air fryer method: Preheat to 400°F. Toss frites with oil and cook in a single layer for 15-20 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through. Salt immediately after cooking. Same principle on timing: get them going so they land with the steak.

Sear the steak: Get your cast iron, carbon steel, or stainless steel pan ripping hot over high heat; go bigger than you think you need. Add a thin film of neutral oil. When it just starts to smoke, lay the steak in away from you.
Start with about 1 minute per side to build your initial crust, then flip every 30 seconds, letting the heat from the pan surface work both sides evenly.

In the last 90 seconds, add butter (2 Tbsp), garlic (2 cloves), and thyme (2-3 sprigs). Tilt the pan and baste continuously. For a thicker steak, once you have the crust you want, either keep basting to finish or transfer the pan to a 225°F oven.
Pull when your thermometer reads 125-128°F for medium-rare. Rest, preferably on a wire rack, for at least 5-8 minutes.
Build the bordelaise: In the same pan the steak cooked in, over medium heat, add the shallot (1 medium) and minced garlic (2 cloves) and cook 2-3 minutes until softened and picking up the fond.
Deglaze with the red wine (2 cups), scraping the bottom of the pan thoroughly. Reduce over high until almost au sec; you're looking for a syrupy, concentrated glaze coating the bottom of the pan.
Add the beef stock (2 cups) and reduce again until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

Strain the sauce into a small saucepan, pressing on the solids to get everything out. Off heat, add the bone marrow (1/4 cup) and blend with an immersion blender until fully emulsified and glossy. Taste and adjust salt.
Plate: Slice the steak against the grain. Spoon the bordelaise generously over the top. Serve immediately with the frites alongside.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Steak frites with bone marrow is a classic French bistro and brasserie combination.

title: Fennel Salad
steps: On a mandoline, slice the fennel bulb and the red onion. Cut the seeded cucumber into medium pieces.
Remove the peel and the white pith from the blood orange and the grapefruit, cut out the segments and set aside.
Remove the pits from the dates and roughly chop them.
Put everything in a large bowl. Add salt, pepper and the paprika, olive oil, mint leaves and fresh dill. Mix well. Serve.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Originally from Sicily, fennel salad usually is paired with oranges.

title: Marbled Pumpkin Cheesecake
description: Creamy cheesecake and pumpkin layers with beautiful swirls, topped with a light cream cheese frosting and a drizzle of caramel. A soft, delicate dessert perfect for fall.

ingredients.raw: 454 g (16 oz) organic cottage cheese (I used organic farmer's cheese with no excess liquid. It has a thick, firm consistency. If your cheese contains too much moisture, I recommend straining it before using it in the recipe) (cheesecake layer)
80 g (1/3 cup + 1 tbsp) granulated sugar (cheesecake layer)
400 g (about 1 3/4 cups) pumpkin purée (canned or homemade from roasted pumpkin) (pumpkin layer)
70 g (about 1/2 cup + 1 tbsp) powdered sugar (pumpkin layer)
150 g (2/3 cup) cream cheese (cream cheese frosting)
100 g (about 1/3 cup + 1 tbsp) heavy cream, chilled (cream cheese frosting)
50 g (1/3 cup + 1 tbsp) powdered sugar (cream cheese frosting)

steps: Blend the cottage cheese, eggs, sugar, and cornstarch until creamy. Stir in the poppy seeds.
In another bowl, blend the pumpkin purée, eggs, cornstarch, and powdered sugar until smooth.
Line a baking pan with parchment paper. Alternately spoon both mixtures into the center, about 2 tbsp at a time, creating concentric layers.
Bake at 340°F (170°C) for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the edges are set and the center has a slight jiggle. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, vanilla, and powdered sugar until smooth. Add the cold heavy cream and whip again until light and fluffy.
Spread or pipe the frosting over the cooled cheesecake. Finish with a drizzle of caramel sauce, if desired. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: American chains like The Cheesecake Factory and Starbucs serve this as a season item arounfd fall.

title: Tartiflette

ingredients.raw: 1 Reblochon, halved horizontally (1 half diced and folded into the mix and 1 half placed on top before baking)

steps: Cook the lardons until they render their fat and start getting crispy, then add the finely chopped onions. Let them caramelize.

Deglaze with the white wine, then add the crème fraîche, salt and pepper. Add the crozets, then cube half of the Reblochon and add it to the mix. Pan cook for a few minutes, then transfer to an oven-safe dish.
Add the rest of the Reblochon on top of the mix. Bake at 200°C for 20 to 30 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden brown.

cultural relevance.reasoning: The dish has Protected Designation of Origin in Reblochon. This is a modified version of the original recipe.

title: Mussels Tomato Pasta
steps: Finely chop the shallot and garlic and cook them in olive oil. Add the red jalapeño and basil. Cook until aromatic, then add salt, the cherry tomatoes (halved) and the yellow tomato (roughly chopped). Zest the lemon and add it to the mix. Let it cook for a minute or two.
Add 1/2 cup of white wine and the mussels (thoroughly washed beforehand!). Cook until the alcohol evaporates and the mussels open.
Add your pasta (very al dente, as it finishes cooking in the mussel and tomato mix), adding pasta water as needed. Add parsley and salt to taste.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Mediterrnean countries gain access to tomatoes through Columbian exchange. The tomato-shelfish pairing happened in Spain and Italy.

title: Steak Yuzu Kosho

ingredients.raw: steak (from the steps; no ingredient list)
salt (from the steps; no ingredient list)
pepper (from the steps; no ingredient list)
oil (for searing) (from the steps; no ingredient list)
green onions (greens and whites) (from the steps; no ingredient list)
olive oil (from the steps; no ingredient list)
ao-kosho (from the steps; no ingredient list)
lime juice (from the steps; no ingredient list)
white rice (to serve) (from the steps; no ingredient list)

steps: Rest the steak overnight, uncovered, in the fridge (it should be dry so it gets crispy later on).
Salt and pepper it, sear it in a really hot pan with oil, and cook as normal.
Separately, chop the green onions (greens and whites) and add olive oil, the ao-kosho and the lime juice. This is the salad that will accompany the steak.
Serve the steak with freshly made white rice and the kosho green onions.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Yuzu kosho originated in the Kyushu region of South Japan. Pairing the paste with steak briges regional Japanese mountain preservation techniques with modern cuisine.

title: Potato Egg Stacked Breakfast

ingredients.raw: green onions (green and white) (from the steps; for the guacamole)
a teaspoon chilli oil (from the steps)

steps: Grate the potato, add salt and let it sit for a few minutes. The potato should release some water. Use a cheesecloth to squeeze out as much water as possible.
In a hot pan, add oil and butter (1 teaspoon each) and lay the potato hash brown in a pancake shape.
Chop the green onions (green and white).
Cook the bacon strips until crispy.
Mix the avocado, green onions, lime juice, salt and cilantro to make guacamole.
Pan-fry an egg using a teaspoon of chilli oil; add salt and pepper to taste.
Assemble: lay down the potato pancake first, then the egg, then a dollop of guacamole and a slice of crispy bacon. Enjoy!

title: Courgette and Sausage Pasta
steps: Chop the courgettes and fry them with garlic and chilli; add salt.
Cook the sausage in the same oil, add the chopped shallot and garlic, and deglaze with the wine. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add the pasta, pasta water, basil, lemon zest, and the fried courgettes. Garnish with the parmigiano reggiano.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In some regions of Italy pork sausage (salsiccia) is a staple pasta accompaniment.

title: Kimchi Grilled Cheese & Roasted Tomato Soup

ingredients.raw: Tomatoes (15 - I used a mix of regular and vine tomatoes) (soup)
Red pepper (2, I used sweet peppers) (soup)

steps: Seed the peppers and roughly chop them along with the tomatoes and onion. Halve the whole head of garlic. Arrange everything on a baking tray with the basil stems, then drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Bake at 200°C for 30 to 45 minutes.
Transfer all of it (including the released juices) to a pan. Add the stock and the garlic, squeezed out of its peel. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Blend, return to the pan, and add the tomato puree, a few dashes of Worcestershire sauce, chilli flakes, salt, pepper and the double cream, all to taste, plus a little sugar if it is too acidic. Let it cook on low while you make the grilled cheese.
For the grilled cheese: on the bread, layer cheese, kimchi and more cheese, with salt and pepper to taste.
Put it into a buttered pan with a weight to press it down. Wait until it's crispy, then turn it and repeat the weight method.
Serve together and enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Kimchi is a foundational symbol of Korean identity. Here it is accompanying grilled cheese, a staple american comfort food, and tomato soup.

title: Ultimate High Protein Chicken & Egg Salad Smash

ingredients.raw: buttered sourdough (to serve, from the method)
buttered sourdough (to serve, from the method)
chilli crisp oil (to serve, from the method)

steps: In a large bowl, mix all the sauce ingredients until well combined.
Add the shredded chicken, boiled eggs, green onions, sun-dried tomatoes, chopped gherkins, dill and parmesan.
Smash until well combined and creamy. It's ready to eat.
To serve on toast: top buttered sourdough with scoops of the chicken and egg smash salad, chilli crisp oil and furikake.
To serve as a wrap: add the chicken and egg smash salad to a tortilla, wrap it up, and toast it for a couple of minutes on both sides.

title: Bluefin Tuna Tartare

ingredients.raw: 3 steaks of bluefin tuna (from the steps)
a teaspoon of capers (from the steps)
a teaspoon of dijon mustard (from the steps)
a few dashes of worcestershire sauce (from the steps)
2 teaspoons of extra virgin olive oil (from the steps)

steps: Finely cube 3 bluefin tuna steaks and add them to a bowl.
Finely chop 2 shallots and add them to the tuna bowl. Finely chop 7 small dill pickles and add them to the bowl.
Finely chop a teaspoon of capers and add them to the bowl.
Add a teaspoon of Dijon mustard, a few dashes of Worcestershire sauce, salt, MSG and Tabasco sauce. Add 2 teaspoons of extra virgin olive oil and one egg yolk. Mix. Set aside to chill in the fridge.
Slice 3 small potatoes on a mandoline, then cut them into matchsticks. Rinse in ice-cold water to remove some starch, then carefully fry them, salting them as soon as they're out of the oil.
Serve the tuna topped with the fries and sprinkled with chives. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: French bistro technique popularized in Los Angeles in the 80s.

title: Homemade Spiced Pear Liqueur
description: It's well worth making because it turns out delicious, I promise; you just need patience, haha.

ingredients.raw: 2 ripe pears, washed and chopped, cored and seeded
100 g light brown sugar, about 0.5 cup firmly packed (for the syrup)
1 tiny pinch of salt (for the syrup)

steps: Add the pears, vodka and brandy to a clean glass jar. Close it and let it macerate for five days in a cool, dark place. Use spirits of about 40% alcohol.
On the fifth day, add the cinnamon, cardamom and clove. Leave it one more night, tasting from 12 hours on so the spices don't overpower the pear.
Strain, and if you want to remove the finer particles, also pass it through a coffee filter.
For the syrup: heat the brown sugar and the pinch of salt with the water in a small pot over low heat until dissolved, then let it cool completely. This makes more than the 100 ml you will use.
Add the vanilla and 100 ml of the finished syrup to the strained liqueur. Mix and taste; if you want it sweeter, add a little more.
Bottle it and keep it in the fridge. You can taste it right away, but I recommend letting it rest for a couple of days so the flavors come together.

title: Sardines, Smashed Cannellini and Herb Dressing on Rye Bread
description: This is a little snack or light lunch I really love! It's not the prettiest but it's sooo yummy and super healthy! Also done with things you probably have somewhere in your cupboard! Give it a go!
steps: Chop the shallots, capers and parsley. Mix with salt, olive oil, chilli flakes, lemon juice and lemon zest.
In a pan, fry the beans in olive oil. Add garlic, salt, pepper and lemon zest. Slightly smash them to get a purée-like consistency.
Spread onto the bread and top with the sardines, the shallot-caper dressing and more lemon zest. Enjoy!

title: Miso Aubergine + Sesame Chickpea Platter
description: 96% of people in the UK + America don't get enough fibre. The recommended daily amount is around 30g - and as a general rule, the best sources of fibre out there are - you guessed it - plants! Dietary fibre is SUPER important for maintaining a healthy, balanced lifestyle. Among other things, it helps improve digestion, regulate blood sugar AND supports a healthy gut.

ingredients.raw: 2 small aubergines (I used Chinese/Japanese aubergines) (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tbsp white miso paste (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tbsp soy sauce (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tsp minced garlic (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tsp minced ginger (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tsp maple syrup (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 tbsp sunflower / neutral oil (for the aubergine + glaze)
1 brown onion, finely sliced (for the chickpeas)
2 large garlic cloves, finely sliced (for the chickpeas)
1/2 red chilli, finely chopped (for the chickpeas)
570g jar chickpeas + their liquid (for the chickpeas)
1 tsp toasted sesame oil (for the chickpeas)
a good glug of olive oil (from the steps)
a pinch of salt (from the steps)

steps: Pre-heat the oven (or use an air fryer) to 180°C fan. Make the marinade in a small bowl by whisking together the miso paste, soy sauce, oil, garlic, ginger + maple syrup.
Slice the aubergines in half and score the flesh with a small knife, then place them onto a roasting tray and brush generously with the marinade.
Roast for around 20-25 minutes, checking halfway + brushing with a little more oil / marinade if needed, and cook until beautifully golden and the flesh soft.

Meanwhile, get your chickpeas going. Get a good glug of olive oil in a frying pan on a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the onion with a pinch of salt, and allow to soften for 3-4 minutes. Lower the heat slightly, add the garlic + chilli, then fry for a further minute until fragrant.

Add the chickpeas with their liquor and a splash of sesame oil. Mix, then bubble away on a medium heat for around 10 minutes, stirring every now + then to avoid burning. Season to taste with a good squeeze of lime juice to finish.

Once your aubergines have softened completely, it's time to build your platter. Spoon on the chickpeas, pop the roasted aubergines on top, then finish with sliced chilli, spring onions, coriander, toasted sesame seeds + lime wedges.

cultural relevance.reasoning: This dish is insparied in Japanese Nasu Dengaku, a classic dish from the Muromachi period.

title: Calpico

ingredients.raw: a liter and a half of water (mineral or still) (from the steps)

steps: In a large container, stir the condensed milk, sugar and the juice of the limes until combined. Add the yogurt and the vanilla.
Stir and add a liter and a half of water (mineral or still) and ice.
Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Known as caplis in Japan. A fermented milk very commonly consumed in school lunches.

title: Caramelised Onion, Sun-Dried Tomato + Brown Butter Pasta
description: The beauty of this particular pasta recipe is that we're using just a handful of simple, store-cupboard ingredients that you'll most likely have knocking around at home already. It's a great example of maximising flavour with relatively minimal effort. Now you could absolutely whip this up in no time at all, but I'd highly recommend allowing your onions, which are of course the star ingredient, plenty of time to caramelise properly. I'm talking low and slow until they turn a beautifully dark, golden brown colour. It should take about half an hour or so, and I promise you it's worth it. The natural sweetness they release, alongside the nutty notes of the browned butter, really does provide a brilliant flavour base.

ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp nutritional yeast (or vegetarian hard cheese)
200g pasta of choice - I like mafaldine (+ pasta water)
To garnish: chilli oil, fresh chives
To garnish: chilli oil, fresh chives
a large pinch of salt (from the steps)

steps: Slice your onions in half. Then, with the flat side down, slice them into half moons. Warm a splash of olive oil in a large saucepan / casserole dish on a medium-high heat, then melt in the butter. Allow it to foam + brown, stirring regularly (2-3 minutes).

Add the onions with a large pinch of salt. Cook on a medium heat, stirring regularly + adding a splash of water if sticking, until golden, softened + caramelised (at least 20-30 mins - the longer the better). We want the onions to be sticky + dark brown.

Mince the garlic + finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes. Once the onions have caramelised, add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes + chilli flakes. Stir to combine + cook for a further two minutes. Season with black pepper.
Get your pasta on to boil in salted water. Cook until just al dente, reserving a bowl of pasta water.

Briefly remove the sauce from the heat, then pour in the cream + add the nutritional yeast, and stir well to combine. Allow to bubble away on a low heat whilst your pasta cooks, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen.

Add the drained pasta to the sauce with a ladle of pasta water. Stir + toss well to finish cooking the pasta, adding another ladle of pasta water to create a creamy, emulsified sauce that coats the pasta completely.

Add the finely chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice, then get the pasta into bowls. Spoon over any leftover sauce, then finish with a drizzle of good olive oil (I like garlic or chilli oil here) + more parsley or chives if using - enjoy!

title: Creamy Pumpkin Gnocchi
description: Boy do I have a special recipe for you today... and it couldn't have come at a better time. I'm not sure about you guys, but where I am in the UK, it's definitely getting colder, wetter and darker by the day.

ingredients.raw: 1 large garlic bulb, sliced in half
300ml vegetable stock (+ more to loosen, to preference)
400g extra firm (smoked) tofu, crumbled into small pieces
Splash of cider vinegar (optional), to taste
Large handful fresh parsley, leaves finely chopped
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted pumpkin seeds, swirl of cream, fresh parsley
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted pumpkin seeds, swirl of cream, fresh parsley
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted pumpkin seeds, swirl of cream, fresh parsley
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted pumpkin seeds, swirl of cream, fresh parsley

steps: Pre-heat your oven to 180°C fan (or use an air fryer). Slice the tops off your munchkin pumpkins and scoop out the seeds and flesh. Keep the seeds for later! Pop the onion and garlic inside the pumpkins, season with salt + pepper, then the paprika, cumin, dried oregano + turmeric. Drizzle generously with olive oil to fully coat. Pop the pumpkin lids back on + roast for around 30-40 minutes, or until the pumpkin flesh is completely soft and the onion/garlic is cooked.

While the pumpkins roast, crumble the smoked tofu into small pieces. Heat a good splash of olive oil in a frying pan on a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the tofu and fry, without moving, for around 3-4 minutes, until it starts to turn golden-crisp. Season well with salt + pepper, then mix + continue frying for a further 5 minutes until browned all over. Remove from the heat.
Pat the pumpkin seeds dry, season with a pinch of salt + pepper, then drizzle with a splash of oil. Mix well to coat, then pop them in the oven for the final 10 minutes that your pumpkins roast.

Allow the roast pumpkin to cool briefly, then carefully scoop out the flesh into a large saucepan (or straight into a large blender) with the onion, and squeeze out the garlic. Add the coconut milk and vegetable stock, then, either in your blender or using a stick blender, blitz until completely smooth + creamy. Loosen here with a little more stock if needed - you want the texture to be a thick soup.
On a medium-high heat, bring the sauce to a bubble, then add the gnocchi and cook for a minute or two until just al dente, adding a little more stock to cover + loosen as required.
Stir through the miso paste, nutritional yeast, chopped fresh parsley and vinegar if using, then a splash of cream + your crispy tofu. Taste and adjust the seasoning to preference.
To serve, spoon the gnocchi into bowls and finish with another drizzle of cream, toasted pumpkin seeds, fresh parsley + chilli crisp - enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Italy's comfort food during fall, it has now become a social media classic.

title: Moqueca My Way
description: With Brazil in the headlines this week, it felt like the perfect time to revisit a recipe I first made over the summer for Flavours of the World Cup! Now, if you remember that series, you'll know I was having a lot of fun exploring dishes from different countries and giving them my own plant-based twist. And one recipe that I've been meaning to bring back to the table is MOQUECA.

ingredients.raw: 1 butternut squash, peeled + finely chopped into 1cm cubes
2 red or yellow peppers, finely sliced
Small knob of fresh ginger, minced
400g tin cherry tomatoes (or 2 large tomatoes, roughly chopped)
Small handful fresh coriander, to serve
Olive or coconut oil, salt + pepper
Olive or coconut oil, salt + pepper
Olive or coconut oil, salt + pepper

steps: Roast the squash. Preheat your oven (or air fryer) to 180°C fan. Toss the butternut squash with a generous drizzle of olive oil, salt + pepper. Roast for around 15 minutes, shaking halfway through, until tender and beginning to brown.

Start the base. Heat a good glug of oil in a large casserole dish over a medium-high heat. Add the onion + peppers with a pinch of salt and fry for around 5 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic, ginger + chilli, then cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Make the sauce. Pour in the tomatoes, coconut milk and vegetable stock. Bring everything to a gentle bubble, then reduce the heat to low.

Bring it all together. Add the roasted squash, stirring well, then carefully add the tofu. Season with the vegan fish sauce, lime juice, salt + pepper. Pop a lid on and simmer gently for around 15 minutes, occasionally spooning the sauce over the tofu so it absorbs all those lovely flavours. Add a splash of boiling water if the sauce gets a little too thick.
Finish + serve. Scatter over a generous handful of fresh coriander and serve hot, ideally with rice or some lovely bread to mop up that sauce. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Moqueca is a Brazilian seafood stew that depicts the cultural blending of Indigenous, African, and Portuguese traditions.

title: Courgette, Pea & Basil Soup
description: This week's bowl is all about courgettes (known as zucchini to many of you). We're coming to the end of their season here in the UK, so it's time to make the most of them while we still can! If your garden, allotment or vegetable drawer is currently overflowing with them, or indeed you can still find locally grown ones in supermarkets or grocery stores, this is the soup recipe for you...

ingredients.raw: Large bunch of fresh basil, leaves picked + stalks finely chopped
Glug of cider / white wine (or 1 tbsp cider vinegar)
800ml vegetable stock (+ a little more if needed)
1 tsp white miso paste (dissolved in splash of stock / hot water)
Extra virgin olive oil, sea salt & black pepper
Extra virgin olive oil, sea salt & black pepper
Extra virgin olive oil, sea salt & black pepper

steps: Start with the onions: In a large saucepan or casserole dish, warm a good glug of olive oil on a medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and spring onion, season with a good pinch of salt + sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened.

Add the courgettes: Add the chopped courgettes and season with another pinch of salt + a crack of black pepper. Cook for around 5 minutes, stirring every now + again, until the courgettes have softened + have begun to colour. Add the chopped garlic and basil stalks and cook for another minute. Once you have a nice bit of caramelisation, deglaze with a splash of cider (or wine, vinegar or water). Scrape well + allow to cook off for a minute or two.
Add the stock: Pour in the vegetable stock and allow to bubble away for 5 minutes, until the courgettes are completely tender.

Add the peas: Chuck in the frozen peas, chop the basil leaves (reserve a few for garnish) and add them, then stir well + cook for another 1-2 minutes, until the peas are tender. Remove a couple of spoonfuls for garnish.

Blend: Using a hand blender (or whatever you have!), blend the soup until creamy + smooth. I like to do this 3/4 of the way so I get a few chunkier pieces of veg, but this is personal preference; it's up to you how smooth you like it! Stir through most of the cream cheese, the dissolved miso paste and nutritional yeast. Grate in the zest of 1/2 a lemon, then taste + check for seasoning.

Serve: In a small bowl, mix together the reserved peas + chopped basil with a good glug of extra virgin olive oil + the juice of your lemon. Season with salt + pepper, then ladle the soup into bowls + drizzle the pea mix over. Finish with a dollop of cream cheese if you like.

title: Spicy Sweetcorn Tom Kha
description: The most wonderful time of the year is here... SOUP SEASON IS BACK! As we head into autumn, I'll be sharing a brand new soup recipe each week - right here on The Veg Table. We've got one pot soups, one tray soups, lazy ramens and all sorts more. The focus of all these recipes is getting as much veg, fibre, and flavour into our soup as possible, but keeping things nice and simple too.

ingredients.raw: 1 small piece fresh ginger, roughly chopped
1 stalk lemongrass, woody ends removed, bashed + roughly chopped
200g block medium firm tofu, chopped into 1cm cubes
Small handful fresh coriander, leaves finely chopped

steps: Prepare the corn: Shuck the corn if required, then carefully chop in half if needed. Parboil the corn on the cobs for around 2 minutes, then leave to cool slightly.

Fry your aromatics: Whilst your corn cools, prepare your aromatics. On a medium-high heat, warm the oil in a large saucepan. Add the shallot, garlic, ginger, lemongrass and chilli and fry for a few minutes until soft and fragrant. Add the Thai curry paste and cook for another minute or two.

Build your soup: Add your hot stock and coconut milk, bring everything to a gentle simmer + bubble away for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, carefully slice your corn from the cob + roughly chop. Add the sweetcorn and cook for 2-3 more minutes until completely tender.

Blend: Depending on the strength of your blender (stick or bullet blender), you may want to remove the lemongrass here. Blend until completely creamy and smooth, then season with the juice of 1 lime and vegan fish sauce.
Add your protein + veg: Get your cubed tofu and mushrooms into the broth, then pop the lid on + cook for around 5-7 minutes until softened. Check the broth for seasoning, then get ready to serve!
Serve: Ladle the Tom Kha into bowls and finish with coriander, chilli crisp, a squeeze of lime + anything else you fancy. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Tom kha is a traditional Thai coconut-galangal soup. In this case, there's a modern fusion happening by adding sweet corn.

title: Pad Thai Salad
description: All my favourite parts of a Pad Thai - but kept plant-based, slightly lighter + thrown into a salad.

ingredients.raw: 1 tsp fresh ginger, minced (for the dressing)
1 large garlic clove, minced (for the dressing)
1 tsp vegan fish sauce (for the dressing)
1 tsp rice wine vinegar (for the dressing)
200g block extra firm tofu, chopped into 1cm cubes (for the salad)
Large handful fresh coriander / mint / cress (for the salad)
Large handful fresh coriander / mint / cress (for the salad)
Large handful fresh coriander / mint / cress (for the salad)
2 spring onions, finely sliced (for the salad)

steps: Make the dressing: Add the peanut butter, minced garlic, ginger, tamarind, soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, vegan fish sauce, sesame oil, sriracha, maple syrup and the juice of 1/2 a lime to a bowl. Whisk to combine and check for seasoning. If it's a little thick, add a splash of water until you have a nice pourable dressing. You'll use some of it to glaze the tofu too!

Get the tofu crispy: Cut your tofu into small cubes. Heat the coconut oil in a pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the tofu and cook for a few minutes on each side until golden and crispy. Once the tofu is looking good, pour in 1-2 tbsp of your dressing and toss everything together to glaze. Let it cook for another minute or so, allowing the sauce to cling to the tofu and get sticky.

Prep: Soak or cook your rice noodles according to the packet instructions. Give them a little chop with scissors or a knife so they're not all in huge strands - this means they can really soak up all that dressing. Chop your spring onions and roughly chop the peanuts too.

Assemble: Add the noodles, herbs or cress, crispy glazed tofu, spring onions, peanuts, chilli if using, beansprouts + shallots to a big bowl. Pour over the remaining dressing and mix everything together really well. Serve as is, or on a big platter or in bowls. Finish with more peanuts, crispy shallots + spring onion / herbs. Then tuck in!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Pad thai is culturally significant as a symbo, od modern Thai notionality. In this case, we're seeing the salad version of it.

title: Easy Sushi Salad
description: If you love sushi but can't be bothered with all the rolling, this one's for you!

ingredients.raw: 250g pre-cooked rice (or around 2 portions of cold, leftover cooked rice) (for the crispy rice)
2 tbsp cooking oil (I used olive) (for the crispy rice)
1 tsp chilli crisp (for the crispy rice)
1 tbsp soy sauce (for the crispy rice)
2 spring onions, finely sliced (for the salad)
Handful fresh radishes, thinly sliced (for the salad)
2 tbsp pickled ginger, sliced (for the salad)
4 tbsp vegan mayo (I used Kewpie) (for the dressing)
1 tsp minced fresh ginger (for the dressing)
1 small garlic clove, minced (for the dressing)

steps: Make the crispy rice: Preheat your oven to 180°C fan (or use an air fryer). Spread the cooked rice onto a lined baking tray. Drizzle over the oil, soy sauce and chilli crisp, then toss to coat. Bake for around 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the rice is golden and crispy around the edges. It will crisp up as it cools.
Prep the salad: Blanch the edamame in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until al dente, then rinse + drain. Dice the avocado and cucumber, and finely slice the spring onions, radishes and pickled ginger.
Prep the dressing: Whisk together the mayo, chilli crisp, ginger and garlic. Squeeze in the lime juice (start with 1/2, then taste before adding more), then loosen with a splash of water if needed.

Assemble: Get the veg, crispy rice and dressing into a big bowl. Carefully toss together to fully coat, then serve either on a sharing platter or in bowls. Finish with crispy onions + more dressing if you like - enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Sushi is a cultural symbol of Japan. It embodies national identity and the pursuit of perfection. In this case, it's presented in salad form.

title: Burrito Salad
description: If you're looking for something fresh, full of fibre, protein AND packed with flavour, I think you're going to love this...

ingredients.raw: 1 x 300g block extra firm tofu (for the salad)
1 large garlic clove, minced (for the salad)
1 x 400g tin black beans, drained and rinsed (for the salad)
2 corn on the cobs, boiled (or 1 x 200g tinned sweetcorn) (for the salad)
1 small head romaine lettuce, shredded (for the salad)
200g cherry tomatoes, finely diced (for the salad)
1/2 red onion, finely diced (for the salad)
Small handful fresh coriander, leaves finely chopped (for the salad)
Large handful tortilla chips, crushed (for the salad)
Juice of 1/2 lime (more to taste) (for the dressing)
Small handful fresh coriander, leaves finely chopped (for the dressing)
Salt, pepper + olive oil (for frying + drizzling)
Salt, pepper + olive oil (for frying + drizzling)
Salt, pepper + olive oil (for frying + drizzling)

steps: Cook the tofu: Pre-heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add a good glug of olive oil. Pat the tofu dry, then crumble it into mince-like pieces. Add the tofu, season well with salt + pepper, then fry for around 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden-crisp. Add the garlic and chipotle paste, stir well + cook for another minute until fragrant. Add a splash of water to clean the bottom of the pan.
Prepare the beans: Add the drained black beans to a bowl with the juice of one lime, a generous pinch of salt and plenty of black pepper. Mix well and set aside.
Prep the pico de gallo: Dice the tomatoes, red onion, chilli and coriander.
If boiling your own corn, do so until the kernels are nice + yellow, then carefully slice them from the cob.

Make the dressing: Whisk together the yoghurt, 1 clove of minced garlic, 1/2 tsp of chipotle paste, lime juice, and nutritional yeast until combined. Season to taste + loosen with a splash of water if needed.

Assemble: Add the shredded lettuce, black beans, sweetcorn, crispy tofu and pico de gallo ingredients to a large bowl. With your hands, crush the tortilla chips on top, then pour over the creamy chipotle dressing and toss everything together until well coated. Finish with more crushed tortilla chips + coriander, then serve immediately!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Burritos are a symbol of working class resilience in the boarderland across north Mexico and south USA. In this case is presented as a salad.

title: Bánh Mì Salad
description: Pan-fried tofu with a ginger-soy glaze, crunchy veg, fresh herbs, baguette croutons + spicy sriracha mayo. All the best bits of a Bánh Mì, but in salad form!

ingredients.raw: Large handful fresh mint, leaves picked
Large handful fresh coriander, leaves picked
Cooking oil (olive, sunflower), salt, pepper + msg
Cooking oil (olive, sunflower), salt, pepper + msg
Cooking oil (olive, sunflower), salt, pepper + msg
Cooking oil (olive, sunflower), salt, pepper + msg
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted sesame seeds
To serve: chilli crisp, toasted sesame seeds

steps: Pre-heat your oven or air fryer to 200°C fan. Rip the baguette into small, bite-sized pieces. In a mixing bowl, season with a good pinch of salt, pepper, msg + a drizzle of oil. Toss well to coat, then roast for around 10 minutes until golden-crisp.

Using a mandoline or sharp knife, slice the cucumber + carrot into thin diagonal rounds. (I forgot to quick pickle these, so I'd recommend squeezing over the juice of a lime + a good pinch of salt, then mixing well with your hands.) Finely slice your spring onion + chilli (if using) into thin diagonal rounds too.

Slice the tofu into 1cm thick strips. Heat a good glug of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat, then add the tofu. Season with salt, pepper + a pinch of msg, frying on each side for 3-5 minutes until golden.

Whilst the tofu fries, make the speedy glaze. To a small bowl, add the minced ginger + garlic, soy sauce + rice vinegar. Mix well, then once the tofu is cooked on each side, pour it over the tofu. Cook for another few minutes, turning occasionally, until the tofu is well coated in the glaze.
