For the dressing, simply mix the mayo, sriracha + a squeeze of lime juice in a small bowl. Add a splash of water to loosen.

To serve, roughly chop your tofu, then get everything into a large mixing bowl - veg, croutons, tofu, herbs - then pour over the dressing. Toss everything together, whack into bowls or a platter, garnish with toasted sesame seeds + chilli crisp if you like - and tuck in!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Banh mi is a cultural symbol of Vietnamese resilience and everyday life. In this case it is presented as a salad.

title: Shawarma Salad
description: Everything you love about a shawarma (well, apart from the traditional meaty filling), but in salad form. Crispy smoked tofu strips, meaty roasted mushrooms, a harissa tahini yoghurt, crunchy pickles + flatbread croutons. This salad has it ALL...

ingredients.raw: handful pickled Turkish peppers, finely chopped
1 flatbread / wrap, torn into small pieces
small bunch fresh dill or parsley, leaves finely chopped

steps: Make the shawarma-style tofu + mushrooms: Grab your block of smoked tofu and a sharp knife or vegetable peeler. Finely slice or peel the tofu into thin strips. Slice the portobello mushrooms into thin strips too. Add everything to a bowl and season generously with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, salt and pepper. Add a good glug of olive oil to coat and mix gently until everything is well coated. Pop it all into the air fryer (or a pre-heated oven) at 190°C (fan) and roast for around 15-20 minutes until the tofu is crispy and the mushrooms are nicely caramelised. Give everything a shake halfway through.

Make the dressing: Add the yoghurt, tahini, harissa, the juice of 1/2 a lemon, a good pinch of salt and a crack of black pepper to a bowl and mix. The tahini will make the dressing stiffen up - that's fine! Slowly add a little cold water, whisking as you go, until you have a smooth, pourable dressing. Taste and adjust the lemon, salt or harissa depending on how you're feeling!

Prep the salad: Finely shred the cabbage and red onion, then chop your gherkins and Turkish peppers. At this point, I like mixing the sumac through the onions with a good pinch of salt + a squeeze of lemon juice to lightly pickle!

Make the flatbread croutons: Tear your flatbread into small pieces. Heat a good glug of olive oil in a frying pan on a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the flatbread pieces and fry for 1-2 minutes on each side until golden-crisp. Season with a little salt + a pinch of dried oregano. Pop on a cooling rack + dab with kitchen paper to remove any excess oil. This is also the perfect way to use up flatbread that's been hanging around for a little too long.

Assemble: Chuck the cabbage, tofu + mushroom shawarma pieces, sumac onions, pickles, herbs + flatbread croutons into a large mixing bowl. Pour over plenty of the tahini yoghurt dressing, then mix until everything is well coated + combined. Load onto a plate, platter or bowl, garnish with a sprinkle of sumac + enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Shawarma is a symbol of cultural exchange and hospitality in the Middle East. This recipe presents shawarma as a salad.

title: Japanese-Style Egg Sando
description: Lunchbox time, chapter 2. The week is hard enough without eating sad food. And if this recipe feels like too much effort, honestly, I don't know what else I can do for you. Hard-boiled egg, a good homemade mayonnaise and a few things to liven it up. You mix it all, put it between two slices of bread and your lunchbox is sorted. I don't cut the crusts off the bread because I love them. Am I weird? Who knows. There aren't many rules here. Season it however you like and, above all, be generous with the filling. Little fuss, a bit of dignity and zero need to pay ten euros for a sandwich you didn't really want that much.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs.
Mix the eggs with the homemade mayonnaise, green onion, sesame oil, crispy chili oil, rice vinegar and pepper. Season it however you like.
Put the filling between two slices of bread, and be generous with it. (I leave the crusts on.)
If you want it to arrive at work perfect, pack the filling in the lunchbox and the bread separately, and assemble it there.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Known as tamago sando in Japan.

title: Peanut Butter Rice Krispie Treats
description: They're chewy, crunchy, a little salty, a little sweet, and the chocolate on top is SO good. And the best part? You probably already have everything you need to make them.

ingredients.raw: 1 scoop collagen or unflavored protein powder (optional)
A big spoon full of coconut oil
Dark chocolate chips (optional, but highly recommend)

steps: Add the peanut butter, maple syrup, vanilla, salt, and coconut oil to a bowl. Microwave until the coconut oil is melted (~1 minute). Mix everything together until smooth and combined.
If you're adding collagen or protein powder, mix that in.
Then add your Rice Krispies and stir until they're evenly coated.
Line a pan with parchment paper and pour the mixture in. Press everything down firmly into an even layer.
Melt some dark chocolate and drizzle it over the top.
Pop them in the fridge to set, then cut into squares and enjoy! That's literally it.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Culturally significant in the USA as food innovation.

title: Moussaka
description: This one was SENSATIONAL so I wanted to give you the full recipe description! You have to try it!
steps: Slice the aubergines lengthways into 8-10mm slices. Season lightly with salt and leave for 20-30 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush generously with olive oil and roast at 220°C fan for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway, until soft and deeply golden.
Slice the potatoes into 5mm rounds and rinse. Toss with olive oil and salt and roast at 220°C fan for 15-18 minutes, until lightly golden.
Heat a large pan over high heat. Brown the beef in batches until deeply caramelised. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 7-8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes until darkened. Deglaze with the red wine and scrape up all the browned bits.
Return the beef and add the chicken stock, then the tomatoes and spices.
Simmer uncovered for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich.

Then make the béchamel: Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm milk. Cook for 5-7 minutes until thick. Remove from the heat and stir in the Parmesan and spices. Leave to cool for 5 minutes, then whisk in the egg yolks.
In a deep baking dish, layer: potatoes, half the aubergines, the beef ragù, the remaining aubergines, then the béchamel. Finish with a little extra Parmesan.
Bake at 180°C fan for 40-45 minutes.
Let the moussaka rest for 30-45 minutes before slicing. This is what gives you those beautiful, clean layers. Bon appétit!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Moussaka was first documented in 13-century Arabic cookbooks.

title: Sunday's Roast Chicken (Piri Piri-Inspired)
description: Sunday's roast chicken! Inspired by chicken Piri Piri!

ingredients.raw: garlic cloves (for the marinade) (5 to 6 in the steps)
Juice + zest of 1 lemon (for the marinade)
Juice + zest of 1 lemon (for the marinade)
1 tbsp red wine vinegar (I used sherry) (for the marinade)
1 1/2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (for the marinade)
Plenty of black pepper (for the marinade)
garlic cloves (potatoes) (3 to 4 in the steps)

steps: Bake the bell pepper until charred. Blend it with 5 to 6 garlic cloves, the chillies, smoked paprika, oregano, lemon zest and juice, olive oil, red wine vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Crack the chicken's spine and make small cuts in the chicken so the marinade gets in. Use two thirds of the mix to marinate it for at least 24 hours.
In a baking tray, lay out the potatoes, 3 to 4 garlic cloves and 5 or 6 shallots, and sprinkle with olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper and smoked paprika.
Bake at 220°C for 15 minutes per 500 g of chicken, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C at the thickest part. Baste every 20 minutes with the remaining third of the marinade.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Piri piri is a bird's eye chili sauce that embodies centuries of exchange between the Americas, South Africa, and Protugal. In this cas eit's used for marinating a sunday roast chicken, another culturally significant tradition in the United Kingdom.

title: Flying Dutchman
description: We're taking the viral In-N-Out Flying Dutchman and giving it a lighter twist with 93% lean ground beef, buttery grilled onion buns, melty low fat cheddar cheese, and a light homemade burger sauce. All the burger-night flavor without the traditional bun!

ingredients.raw: 3 large white or yellow onions (you may need extra to get enough thick middle slices)
Pickle juice 1-2T depending how thick you want it (light burger sauce)

steps: Cut thick rounds from the middle of your onions to make your onion buns.
Form your beef into balls, season, and place on a hot skillet. Press flat and add salt and pepper. Let it cook until it looks almost cooked all the way through, then flip.
Add cheddar cheese and let it melt.
Fry your onion slices in butter until golden and tender.
Sandwich your cheesy burger patties between the onion slices, add your light burger sauce, and dig in!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Flying Dutchan is a bunless fast-food item form In-N-Out Burger.

title: Boyfriend Sandwich
description: This sandwich is the reason he calls me "Bobby Flay". The pesto and chicken come from the same creator's separate post (https://www.instagram.com/p/DcIy5nkx2NM/): "For years I have been making pesto this exact same way. Growing up my grandpa would make pesto all the time, it was hands down the best pesto any of us ever had. I have had so many people over the years tell me they hated pesto, and then fall in love with this one. So I hope you enjoy it."

ingredients.raw: 1/2c-1c Freshly Grated Pecorino Romano (my favorite is @publix brand block of pecorino imported from Italy) (pesto)
1/4c-1/2c Good quality Olive Oil (from a dark glass bottle) (pesto)
1/2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, parsley (blackened easy chicken)
1/2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, parsley (blackened easy chicken)
1/2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, parsley (blackened easy chicken)
1/2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, parsley (blackened easy chicken)
1/2t each of garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, parsley (blackened easy chicken)
1 lb of Chicken Breast (breasts sliced in half) (blackened easy chicken)
olive oil (for the pan, from the steps) (blackened easy chicken)

steps: Pesto: Blend the basil, Pecorino Romano, garlic, walnuts and olive oil until smooth.
Chicken: Slice your chicken breasts in half lengthways. Pat all the excess moisture off with a paper towel. Season with all the seasonings listed. Do not add olive oil to the chicken.

Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add your olive oil (this will create a nonstick surface on the pan). Drop your chicken fillets in and cook 2-3 minutes per side until they have the perfect blackened color.

Depending on the thickness of your cutlets, turn the heat to low and keep the chicken in the pan (if it's too hot, slide it off the burner). Continue to cook for another 6-8 minutes, flipping occasionally.
Assemble: Slice the ciabatta loaf and stack it with homemade pesto, burrata, the seared chicken, heirloom tomatoes, and arugula and spinach.

title: Sweet & Spicy Drunken Shrimp Noodles

ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp chili garlic sauce (sweet & spicy sauce)
2 tsp fresh ginger, grated (sweet & spicy sauce)
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp cold water (sweet & spicy sauce)
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp cold water (sweet & spicy sauce)

steps: Cook the noodles according to the package directions.
Whisk together the sauce ingredients except the cornstarch slurry. Reserve about 1/4 cup of sauce for finishing.
Toss the shrimp in the seasonings listed, then sear them in oil for 1-2 minutes per side. Remove.
Sauté the green onion whites, carrots and bell pepper for 1-2 minutes. Add the zucchini for another 30-60 seconds. Remove.
Add the remaining sauce to the pan and simmer 2 minutes. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy.
Add the noodles, veggies and shrimp and toss until coated.
Finish with chopped cilantro, peanuts, green onion tops and a drizzle of the reserved sauce.

title: Truffle Grilled Cheese & Roasted Veggie Tomato Soup

ingredients.raw: Black truffle cheese from @traderjoes (truffle grilled cheese, makes one serving)
Sourdough bread from @traderjoes (truffle grilled cheese, makes one serving)
Salted Butter @tillamook (truffle grilled cheese, makes one serving)
8 Plum Tomatoes (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
1/2 Red Onion (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
1 Red Bell Pepper (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
Handful Basil (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
Garlic Bulb (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
2Tbs Heavy cream (I used @organicvalley) (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
1 cup Chicken Bone Broth (I used @kettleandfire) (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
Olive oil (I used @getgraza) (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
Salt (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)
Pepper (roasted veggie tomato soup, makes 2 servings)

steps: Soup: Quarter all the veggies and place them in a roasting pan. Cut the top off the bulb of garlic and add it to the pan. Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt & pepper. Roast at 375°F for about an hour and a half.
Take all the veggies out and place them in a pot. Add the bone broth, heavy cream and basil. Use an immersion blender to blend until smooth.
Grilled cheese: Heat your pan and melt your butter. Get butter on both sides of your bread. Add the cheese and make your sandwich.
Toast on low heat with a cooking weight on top. Flip after 2-3 minutes on each side.
Serve it up and enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Accessible comfort food.

title: From-Scratch Bone Broth Chicken Noodle Soup
description: I wasn't expecting my Soul Healing Chicken Noodle Soup to go viral. I am incredibly grateful and so happy to welcome so many new people to my page.

ingredients.raw: Roasted chicken carcass (bones, skin, and any drippings) (bone broth)
1 whole head garlic, sliced in half (bone broth)
2 tbsp butter or olive oil (chicken noodle soup)
8 cups homemade bone broth (chicken noodle soup)
2-3 cups shredded roasted chicken (chicken noodle soup)
8 oz egg noodles or any noodle of choice (chicken noodle soup)
1 tsp dried thyme & turmeric (chicken noodle soup)
1 tsp dried thyme & turmeric (chicken noodle soup)
Salt and pepper, to taste (chicken noodle soup)
Salt and pepper, to taste (chicken noodle soup)
Fresh parsley for serving (chicken noodle soup)

steps: Roast the chicken: Preheat your oven to 425°F. Pat the chicken completely dry.
Rub with oil and season generously with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika, and thyme. Place breast side up in a roasting pan or Dutch oven.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F. Let the chicken rest for 15-20 minutes before carving.
Remove all the meat and set it aside for the soup. Save every bone, the skin, and any juices left in the pan.

Make the bone broth: Add the chicken carcass, roasted skin, pan drippings, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, parsley, and apple cider vinegar to a large stock pot. Cover with cold water.
Bring just to a gentle boil, then immediately reduce to a very low simmer. Simmer uncovered for 8-16 hours, occasionally skimming any foam from the surface.
Strain the broth through a fine mesh strainer. Discard the bones and use a hand blender to blend the carrots into the broth to make a gorgeous orange color. Allow the broth to cool.
Make the soup: In a large pot, heat the butter or olive oil over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots, and celery for about 6-8 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic, turmeric and thyme and cook for another minute. Pour in the homemade bone broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the egg noodles and cook according to the package directions. Stir in the shredded roasted chicken during the last few minutes so it warms through without drying out.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice if desired and garnish with chopped parsley.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Multiple countries have a version of chicken soup as a symbol of healing, nourishment, and care provided to someone while they're sick.

title: Crispy Breakfast Tacos
description: Breakfast doesn't have to be boring. This morning I had a little fun in the kitchen. When I was on my weight loss journey I made these every single day. Instead of a regular tortilla, I would use a low carb high fiber one. I would throw in whatever protein I had cooked in my fridge.

ingredients.raw: tortillas (low carb high fiber) (from the steps)

steps: Over medium-high heat, drop the butter, onions and potatoes in the pan. Stir occasionally until lightly golden brown. Add in salt, pepper, paprika and parsley. Cover until almost fork tender.
Add in the zucchini and bell pepper. Cook until done.

In a separate saucepan, drop in a bit more butter and keep it on medium-high heat. This step goes quickly, so keep your eggs constantly moving or they will burn. Push the eggs to opposite sides of the pan until there is no more runny liquid on top.
Place a tortilla on top of the eggs and carefully flip it onto a paper plate. Take that tortilla and carefully slide it back into the saucepan.
Top with shredded cheese and your veggie mixture. Fold one side closed and continue to cook the taco until golden brown. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: In Mexico and Texas these are seen as a symbol of regional identity.

title: Mini Cherry Cobblers
description: Everything is cuter when it's tiny. Mini cherry cobblers with a warm, jammy center + golden crispy topping. And yes, the fresh whipped cream is non-negotiable.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups pitted cherries, fresh or frozen
heavy cream (for the whipped cream topping, from the text)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly butter your two mini Dutch ovens.

Make the cherries: Add the cherries, maple syrup, lemon, vanilla, cornstarch, salt, and cinnamon to a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for about 4-6 minutes, stirring, until the cherries release their juices and the liquid starts to thicken.
Divide the hot cherry filling between the Dutch ovens, leaving some room at the top because they'll bubble.
Top with granola of choice (I used Simply Elizabeth).
Bake uncovered for 22-28 minutes, until the topping is deeply golden and you can see cherry filling bubbling around the edges. If the topping needs more color, give it another 2-3 minutes.
Let them sit 10 minutes before digging in. The filling will thicken as it cools.
For the whipped cream topping, just whip heavy cream. I did not add sugar as the cherries were sweet enough.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Juneteenth heritage in the USA.

title: Roasted Veggie Bake with Jammy Eggs
description: Not quite shakshuka, not quite anything else. Just warm, tomatoey, jammy egg perfection that requires an unreasonable amount of crusty bread.

ingredients.raw: a little cheese, optional (havarti, feta or ricotta) (from the steps)
toasted slices of baguette (to serve) (from the steps)
a little butter (for toasting the baguette) (from the steps)

steps: Dice up your veggies and add them to a square baking dish. Add one teaspoon each of salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and dried parsley. Add in your tomato paste and about a tablespoon of EVOO. Mix thoroughly together.
Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes, then stir around and (carefully) pop all the cherry tomatoes. Bake for an additional 30 minutes or until everything is smooshy and falling apart.

Take it out of the oven, create 5 wells, and carefully drop your whole eggs into the holes. Top with a little cheese if you wish (I used havarti, but I have used feta or ricotta and it has been beautiful).
Bake for an additional 8-12 minutes, depending on how firm you like your egg yolks.

I paired mine with toasted slices of baguette. Pan toasting them with a little butter really brings out the flavor of the toast. This dish is so incredible and makes the house smell soooo good. I hope you enjoy!

title: Sexy Steak Sandwich
description: This sandwich IS your weekend dinner plan. This was the best thing I ever made.

ingredients.raw: 2 Tbs Mayo of choice (I love @primalkitchenfoods) (horseradish cream aioli)
1 tsp Apple cider vinegar (horseradish cream aioli)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Completely pat dry your sirloin steaks and season generously with salt & pepper.

Get a stainless steel pan or cast iron skillet hot (medium-high heat), then add olive oil once it's already hot (this will prevent sticking). Sear on all sides and slide the pan directly into your hot oven. Cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Take the steak out and immediately rest it on a cutting board. Do not cut into it for at least 15 minutes.

After moving the steak off the pan, put the pan back on the burner and add butter, the onions, and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook the onions on low until caramelized. You might need to add a little water halfway through.
While the onions cook, prepare your cream sauce: mix all the aioli ingredients together and enjoy.
Assemble: slice the steak and add everything inside the ciabatta: the steak, caramelized onions, spring mix, chives and horseradish cream aioli.

title: High Protein Avocado Toast
description: Sometimes all you need is an avocado toast.
steps: Add your egg to boiling water and cook for 7 minutes, then immediately take it out and put it into an ice bath. Wait 2-3 minutes before removing it and peeling the shell off.
Pan-toast the sourdough with butter.
Assemble your bread with the cottage cheese, avocado and jammy egg, and add a squeeze of lemon to the top along with salt & pepper. Add some chopped parsley for color.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Very popular in California and Australian café culture after the 2010s.

title: Black Cherry French Toast Stuffed Crepes
description: These tasted so good you literally cannot tell the difference between this and a real crepe.

ingredients.raw: Honey (a tbs for the cherry mixture and a tsp for the whipped cream, per the steps)

steps: On a plate, whisk the eggs, a little water, vanilla extract and cinnamon.
Dip a rice paper sheet in the mixture and immediately transfer it to a buttered hot pan. Add a few cherries and seal the top with another dipped rice paper sheet. Set aside. Repeat to make 4 crepes.
Make the cherry mixture in a pot with the cherries, a tbsp of honey and a tsp of cornstarch. Cook until jammy.
For the whipped cream, just beat the cream with a tsp of honey. I mixed some of the cherry mixture in for beautiful color.
Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Creps are part of French culinary heritage.

title: My Version of Chicken Pancit
description: I love this recipe because the amount of veggies (cabbage especially) helps cut the carbs from all the noodles. It's so delicious. It also comes together in under 30 minutes. I hope you enjoy!
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then cook until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Add the garlic, carrots, celery, mushrooms, cabbage and onion to the same pan. Sauté for about 5 minutes, until they begin to soften.
Pour the chicken broth into the skillet and bring to a gentle boil. Add the noodles (uncooked) and cook for about 2 minutes, flipping throughout if necessary so they evenly soak up the broth.
Return the chicken to the pan. Add the soy sauce, umami sauce and black pepper. Toss everything together until evenly coated.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Staple at birthdays, New Year celebrations, and family gatherings in the Philippines.

title: Prawn Rolls
description: These shrimp rolls are the perfect way to end summer.

ingredients.raw: rolls (I made my own brioche rolls) (from the steps)

steps: Bring 2 quarts of water to a boil with the bay leaf, lemon slices and 2 tbsp salt.
Add the shrimp and cook until bright pink and cooked through, about 2 minutes.
Transfer the shrimp immediately to an ice bath. Drain, pat dry and chop into small bite-sized pieces.
Heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the celery, fennel and shallot and cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and let cool.
Add the shrimp, mayo, Worcestershire, Sriracha, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, lemon juice, celery seed, chives and parsley. Mix until combined.
Chill until cold.
Fill each roll with lettuce and about 1/2 cup of shrimp salad. Serve cold.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Goi cuon, in Viertnamise, are often consumed during Lunar New Year for good fortune and prosperity.

title: Healthier Crab Rangoon Dip & Rice Paper Chips
description: Healthier crab rangoon dip & rice paper chips... say no more.

ingredients.raw: rice paper (rice paper chips, from the steps)
soy sauce (rice paper chips, from the steps)
water (rice paper chips, from the steps)

steps: Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth and creamy.
Stir in the imitation crab, mozzarella, scallions, sweet Thai chili sauce, soy sauce, umami sauce, and garlic powder.
Spread into a small baking dish. Top with a little extra mozzarella if you want that bubbly cheese moment.
Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes, then broil for 1-2 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Finish with extra scallions and a drizzle of sweet Thai chili sauce.
Rice paper chips: Mix soy sauce with water, quickly coat the rice paper, stack 2 sheets together, then cut into triangles. Air fry at 375°F until crisp, checking around 5 minutes.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Californian adaptation to a traditional Asian dish.

title: Sweet Potato Banana Blondies
description: Proof that sweet potatoes can literally do anything.

ingredients.raw: 1-2 cups oat or almond flour (add more if needed); consistency needs to be thick as shown in the video, like a dense cake batter
Optional: 1/2 cup white chocolate chips & chopped walnuts
Optional: 1/2 cup white chocolate chips & chopped walnuts

steps: Mix the wet ingredients until smooth, then fold in the dry ingredients + chocolate chips. Spread into a lined 8x8 baking dish.
Bake at 350°F for 50-60 minutes, until just set in the center. Let cool completely.
Whisk together the maple glaze ingredients, adding just enough milk to make it thick but drizzleable. Drizzle all over the cooled blondies, slice + enjoy.

title: Potato Ribboned Chicken Pot Pie
description: When I was a little girl I LOVED getting the Marie Calendar Chicken Pot Pies delivered to our house. I would get home from school and the box would be on our doorstep. I loved them and they're the coziest way to ring in the fall season. Traditional Chicken Pot Pie uses a buttery flaky crust for both the top and the bottom, but potatoes have fewer calories, so I decided to make it this way! PLUS it came out so beautiful. I hope you enjoy! Expect more cozy recipes! xx Alex

ingredients.raw: 1 lb cooked chicken, shredded or chopped (filling)

steps: Heat olive oil and butter in a pan. Add the onions, garlic, carrots, celery, flour and milk. Let it cook for a moment.

As it starts becoming aromatic, add the chicken stock. Let it cook for a few minutes, then add the shredded chicken, the thyme, the blended cottage cheese, the peas, the poultry seasoning and the garlic powder.
Boil and slightly mash all but one of the potatoes.
Separately, in an oven-safe dish, lay the mashed potatoes as if they were a pie crust. Place the cooked chicken filling on top.
Slice the last potato on a mandoline and coat the slices with oil, salt and pepper. Arrange the potato slices like ribbons on top of the chicken.
Bake until the ribbon potatoes are done, about 30 minutes at 200°C.

title: Hidden Veggie Hamburger Helper
description: This creamy, cozy pasta is packed with 6 hidden veggies and you'd genuinely never know. The sauce gets blended until silky smooth, then tossed with ground beef + orecchiette for the ultimate nostalgic comfort meal. All the nostalgic Hamburger Helper energy, just with a whole lot more goodness hiding in the sauce.

ingredients.raw: salt + pepper + seasonings to taste (for the sauce)
salt + pepper + seasonings to taste (for the sauce)
salt + pepper + seasonings to taste (for the sauce)

steps: Roast or sauté your veggies until soft, then blend with the beef bone broth and a splash of cream until completely smooth.
Brown your ground beef and cook the orecchiette until al dente.
Bring everything together with the creamy veggie sauce. Add a splash of pasta water if needed and let it get thick, glossy + cozy.

title: Focaccia Sandwich
description: Homemade focaccia, pesto, mortadella, salami, spicy capocollo, provolone, arugula, tomatoes, burrata, crispy prosciutto, roasted peppers. The sandwich that ruined all other sandwiches for me. Save this for the next time you're hangry.
steps: Toast the focaccia.
Stack it tall: pesto, layered mortadella, salami and spicy capocollo, provolone, arugula and sliced tomatoes, torn burrata, crispy prosciutto and roasted peppers.
Press it down, and try to fit it in your mouth. Good luck.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Focaccia is a traditional Italian oven-baked flatbread.

title: Golden Lemon Chicken Soup
description: This is my cure to ANY cold + flu. A big thank you to @gab_oneill for inspiring me with this soup. She made it for me when I was sick last year, and I swear it cured me.
steps: Add olive oil to a hot Dutch oven, add the whole chicken breasts and brown them on both sides. Season with salt and pepper and set to the side.

Add butter right into the Dutch oven, then add the leeks, onion and garlic. Sauté until slightly browned. Add the celery and carrots, and add the chicken breasts right on top. Add your chicken bone broth and simmer covered for 35 minutes.
Remove the chicken breasts from the soup. Add the juice of 2 lemons, the turmeric and the ginger. Shred the chicken and return it to the pot. Add chopped parsley and the Arborio rice.
Stir occasionally on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the rice is fully cooked. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Multiple countries have a version of chicken soup as a symbol of healing, nourishment, and care provided to someone while they're sick.

title: Sticky Date Pumpkin Spice Rice Pudding
description: Basically fall in a bowl. Warm pumpkin spice rice pudding sweetened with maple syrup, swirled with pumpkin, and topped with gooey caramel-like dates. It's cozy, creamy, naturally sweetened and made with simple ingredients. The kind of dessert that makes your whole kitchen smell like fall.

ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked white rice (for the rice pudding)
2 cups whole milk (for the rice pudding)
1 cup half & half (for the rice pudding)
3/4 cup pumpkin purée (for the rice pudding)
2-3 tbsp pure maple syrup (for the rice pudding)
1 tsp vanilla extract (for the rice pudding)
1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice (for the rice pudding)
Pinch of sea salt (for the rice pudding)
6-8 Medjool dates, pitted and chopped (for the date syrup)
1/3 cup hot water (for the date syrup)
1 tbsp maple syrup (for the date syrup)
Pinch of sea salt (for the date syrup)

steps: Make the pudding: Add the cooked rice, milk, half & half, pumpkin, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg and salt to a saucepan. Simmer over low to medium-low heat for about 20-25 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick, creamy and almost custard-like.

Make the sticky dates: Add the chopped dates and hot water to a small saucepan. Simmer until the dates become very soft. Add the butter, maple syrup and salt, then mash with a fork until you have a thick, gooey date caramel. Add another splash of water if needed.
Make it extra sticky: Swirl about half of the date mixture into the warm rice pudding. Spoon into bowls and finish with the remaining sticky dates on top.
A little tip: Let the pudding sit for 5-10 minutes before serving. It thickens as it cools. If it gets too thick, stir in a splash of milk.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Rice pudding is culturally significant accross multiple cultures. In this case the recipe calls for dates and pumpkin spice, which are also culturally relevant items in the Middle East and the USA respectively.

title: Adult Apple Cheddar Caramelized Onion Grilled Cheese
description: I hope you enjoy! xx
steps: Assemble: add everything inside the sourdough bread: shredded cheddar, sliced apple, caramelized onions and, if you like, hot honey.
Grill the sandwich in a buttered pan over medium heat until golden on both sides and the cheese is melted.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Grilled cheese is a culturally relevant recipe as an accessible comfort food item.

title: Miso Tuna Sushi Cake

ingredients.raw: creamy crab mixture with imitation crab (layer)
2 tbsp white miso (for the miso ginger tuna)
2 tbsp soy sauce (for the miso ginger tuna)
1 tbsp rice vinegar (for the miso ginger tuna)
1 tbsp honey (for the miso ginger tuna)
1 tsp sesame oil (for the miso ginger tuna)
fresh grated ginger (for the miso ginger tuna)
minced garlic (for the miso ginger tuna)

steps: For the miso ginger tuna, mix the white miso, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, fresh grated ginger and minced garlic, and toss with the tuna.

Build the cake in a springform pan. From top to bottom, the layers are: mango + kiwi + cucumber; seasoned sushi rice; cream cheese; seaweed; avocado; miso ginger tuna; another layer of sushi rice; creamy crab mixture with imitation crab; cucumber; a layer of sushi rice.
Pack each layer down firmly as you build, then chill until set.
Release the springform pan and present on a serving plate.

cultural relevance.reasoning: This is a fmodern, usion dish that blends traditional Japanese preservation techniques with dining culture.

title: Better for You Banana Bread
description: This Banana Bread is so amazing and honestly I believe the only recipe my kids will continue to make over and over again. Like a mom's famous banana bread kind of thing. Well, that's kind of what I imagine in my head. It's actually also the only recipe I've ever written in my recipe book because it's so wholesome and so freaking good.

ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup melted coconut oil or unsalted butter
1 3/4 cup whole wheat or oat flour
1/3 cup dark chocolate or semi sweet @lilys_sweets

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan or line it with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mash the 4 ripe bananas until mostly smooth with a few small lumps.
Whisk in the 1/2 cup coconut sugar, 1/3 cup melted coconut oil or butter, 2 large eggs, and 1 tsp vanilla extract until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the 1 3/4 cup whole wheat or oat flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp fine sea salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just combined; don't overmix.
Gently fold in the 1 cup freeze-dried blueberries and the dark chocolate, distributing them evenly through the batter. BARELY EVEN MIX THESE IN - OVERMIXING WILL MAKE THE LOAF TURN GREEN!
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for exactly 55 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let the loaf cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.

Notes: Freeze-dried berries are added whole and dry, straight into the batter, with no need to thaw or rehydrate. They'll soften slightly as they bake but stay distinct instead of bleeding color through the loaf. Store covered at room temp for 2 days, or refrigerate up to a week.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Banana bread represents frugality, comfort, and dometic adaptavility in american households after the Great Depression.

title: Pumpkin Spice Protein Cookie Dough
description: Made with almond flour, creamy almond butter, real pumpkin, maple syrup and chocolate chips. No baking required and dangerously good straight from the fridge.

ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup creamy almond butter or peanut butter

steps: Mix the almond flour, pumpkin, almond butter, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice and salt until thick and creamy.
Fold in the chocolate chips. If you want it firmer and more cookie-dough-like, refrigerate for 30-60 minutes.
Spoon into a jar, top with a few extra chocolate chips and keep refrigerated.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In the USA, during fall, pumpkin spice flavors have blend into a modern seasonal ritual.

title: High Protein Rice Paper Buffalo Chicken Hot Pocket
description: Crispy on the outside, creamy and spicy on the inside. These are ridiculously easy, and high-protein.

ingredients.raw: Rice paper sheets, 2 per hot pocket

steps: Blend the cottage cheese until smooth.

Make the filling. In a large bowl, combine the shredded chicken, blended cottage cheese, Frank's RedHot, cheese, green onion, salt, pepper, and onion powder. Mix until everything is creamy and evenly coated.

Prep the rice paper. Beat the eggs in a shallow dish. Dip 2 rice paper sheets together into the egg wash just until they begin to soften. Don't let them sit too long or they'll become difficult to work with.

Stuff & fold. Place the softened rice paper on a flat surface. Add a generous scoop of buffalo chicken filling to the center. Fold the sides inward, then fold the top and bottom over the filling to create a sealed rectangular "Hot Pocket."
Bake. Place seam-side up on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 450°F for 10 minutes.
Get them crispy. Switch the oven to low broil and broil for about 5 minutes, or until deeply golden and crispy. Keep an eye on them during this step, they can go from golden to scorched fast.
Serve hot with extra buffalo sauce, ranch, or blue cheese dressing for dipping.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Originally from Buffalo, NY, buffalo chicken flavors are a staple of sports bar culture.

title: Bacon Egg and Cheese Stuffed Rice Paper Bagel
description: Everybody needs a bacon egg and cheese stuffed bagel.

ingredients.raw: everything but the bagel seasoning (from the steps)

steps: Dip rice paper sheets into egg wash and lay them on a cutting board.
Lay scrambled eggs, cheese, and bacon, roll into a bagel shape.
Top with everything but the bagel seasoning and then place in an air fryer on 375 for 12-15m depending on how you like the color.

title: Nduja Chickpea Pasta
description: It's that time again, quick one this. Hearty with a little kick, lovely.

ingredients.raw: Parmesan (or other hard Italian cheese) - 20g to 30g

steps: Base - Heat a pan to medium-low, add enough olive oil to coat the bottom of the pan. Break apart the nduja (or dice your spicy sausage if firmer), add to the pan and cook out for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the chickpeas and their water, cook for another minute. Season with salt here if needed but be gentle, my chickpea stock is quite salty, if yours is too bear this in mind. Your sausage is likely well seasoned already too.
Pasta - Prepare your pasta as per packet instructions with salty boiling water, cook slightly under al-dente as we will finish the pasta in the pan with the sauce.

Finishing - Once the pasta is ready, add to the pan with a little pasta water, combine well. On low heat add lemon zest, juice of half the lemon, and half your parsley. Combine again. Finish by adding half your cheese bit by bit, adjusting with pasta water and stirring until everything is coated nicely and the cheese is incorporated. Taste for seasoning, but it's likely already salty enough this one.
Plating - Add the pasta to a plate and top with more parsley and cheese. Enjoy immediately!

cultural relevance.reasoning: In Calabria, Italy, nduja carries a legacy of inexpensive cooking. This is a fusion recipe that incorporates Italian elements.

title: Kaya Toast with Half-Boiled Eggs
description: Rather indulgent breakfast sandwich, beloved in both Singapore and Malaysia.
steps: Kaya: In a pan, slowly reduce the coconut milk into coconut cream at medium-low heat, increasing the viscosity and fat percentage. Take 400ml down to 240ml. This should take 10 to 15 minutes. Don't rush on high heat and don't let the milk reach boiling, otherwise you risk splitting. Set aside.

In a bowl, whisk the eggs until fully combined, pass through a fine sieve, then combine well with 120g sugar until completely dissolved. Slowly heat in the bowl over simmering water while constantly stirring until slightly thickened and uniform. 10 to 15 minutes.

Add the coconut cream and knotted pandan leaves (if using) and continue stirring and heating, don't allow to boil. If you have a thermometer, you're looking to increase the temperature of the mixture to 80°C (180°F) and then keep it between 80°C (180°F) and 90°C (195°F) until it thickens to the point it can coat a spoon like in the video. Around 20 to 30 minutes.

Separately, add 30g of sugar to a saucepan, spread it evenly across the pan. Heat slowly until completely caramelised without stirring. Be careful of burning, a few bubbles are fine like in the video but you want to be careful not to overdo it. Once liquid, pour into the kaya while stirring. It may solidify temporarily but if you keep stirring while hot, it will combine. Season with a small pinch of salt and set aside to cool.

Eggs: Boil some water, then add 2 eggs. Let them sit in the water undisturbed for 6.5 minutes, then remove to cool slightly. Crack open and spoon into a small bowl, season with soy sauce and white pepper.

Kaya toast (2 sandwiches): Toast slices of white bread in butter, then remove the crusts, spread with kaya, add 2 slices of butter to each sandwich and season with salt if your butter is unsalted. Halve each sandwich.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Classic Singaporean breakfast pairing of sweet coconut-egg jam and cold butter on toast served alongside runny soft-boiled eggs seasoned with dark soy sauce and white pepper.

title: Skagen Toast (Skagenröra)
description: A fresh and fancy looking piece of toast. Sweden really got something here. Loved this thing, would make a great starter or canapé.
steps: Prep - Finely dice the onion, zest the lemon, finely chop the herbs. Chop the prawns, sizing is really up to you, it's nice to have some chunks in my opinion. Reserve 4 whole prawns for topping.
Mix - Create the skagenröra by mixing the prawns with the onion, herbs, mayo, creme fraiche, horseradish, lemon zest, white pepper. Season with salt to taste.
Toast - Remove the crusts from your bread and fry in a good amount of butter until golden.
Assemble - Top the toast with the skagenröra, more dill and the whole prawns. If using roe, pop that on top too. Enjoy immediately!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Creamy shrimp salad. In 1956, Tore Wretman was competing in a sailing race near Skagen, at the northern tip of Denmark. When the wind died down and his crew grew discouraged, Wretman improvised a meal from the boat's supplies, whisking eggs and oil into mayonnaise and mixing it with shrimp, dill, and lemon.

title: Middle Eastern Inspired Air Fryer Meatball Tray Bake with Tahini Pistachio Cookie
description: Dinner & dessert in one fell swoop. The @ninjakitchenuk CRISPi DualZone glass air fryer has two hefty glass baskets, letting you cook 2 dishes at once and watch them cook, so you know when they're perfect or need adjusting. P.S. This thing makes a MEAN cookie. The crispy top and gooey bottom contrast is stunning.
steps: Chop and deseed veg; peel and crush garlic. Toss veg with chickpeas, seasonings, salt and 2 tbsp olive oil. Mix all meatball ingredients by hand and shape into 4-5 large balls. Add veg to the air fryer basket, meatballs on top.
Mix all sauce ingredients, taste for seasoning.

Cream butter, tahini and sugars. Mix in egg and vanilla. Stir in flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt, then chocolate and pistachios. Lightly grease the basket base, add cookie mix and level with a spatula.

Roast tray bake at 180°C (360°F) for 30 mins; bake cookie at 160°C (320°F) for 28 mins. Flip meatballs and veg at 10 and 20 mins. Remove meatballs once fully cooked at around 20 mins. For a super crisp cookie top, raise to 180°C (360°F) for the last 5 mins. Rest cookie 10 mins before eating.
Serve tray bake with sauce, pomegranate seeds and chopped mint. Top cookie with vanilla ice cream and more pistachios.

title: Peach Danishes with Whipped Crème Fraîche Custard
description: Peach danishes filled with peach compote and crème fraiche custard, topped with poached peaches. The pastry is the Natasha's Baking croissant dough (yeast method): https://natashasbaking.com/croissant-yeast-method/

ingredients.raw: 205 g pastry roll-in butter, 82% fat or higher (butter block)
pie weights, lentils, beans or rice (from the steps)
reserved poached peach halves (from the steps)
simple syrup: equal parts sugar and water (from the steps)
simple syrup: equal parts sugar and water (from the steps)

steps: Croissant dough, the night before: dissolve the yeast in the water and milk, then mix in the sugar, salt and flour only until combined; the dough can stay a bit lumpy. Refrigerate overnight.
Shape the butter into a flat square in parchment and chill it briefly so it is cold but still pliable.
Roll the dough into a square, set the butter in the center and seal the dough around it.
Laminate: roll and fold the dough into three letter folds, chilling about an hour between folds.

Carefully cut a small cross in the peaches, then briefly boil them so the skin separates. Remove the peel and halve them. Reserve one half, and chop the other into small squares to make a peach compote with the sugar and lemon; cook until the peaches are soft.

Roll out the croissant dough and cut it into squares. Proof until doubled and jiggly (4-5 hours at about 24-26°C) and brush with egg wash. Make a small round hole in the center of each with a weighted, oven-safe dish filled with pie weights (lentils, beans or rice can be used). Bake as normal: 190°C (375°F) for 25-30 minutes until deep golden.

Whipped crème fraîche custard: cook the milk, egg yolks, sugar and cornstarch until you have a thick custard. Remove from the heat and whisk in the crème fraîche and vanilla. Chill completely, then lightly whip until smooth and airy.
Once the pastry is cold, spoon in the peach compote and pipe the whipped crème fraîche custard on top.

Finally, add the other peach half on top to decorate. Glaze it with vanilla paste and simple syrup (vanilla, equal parts sugar and water, blended on high), covering the peach, and sprinkle with powdered sugar. Serve.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In 1850, a strike among Danish bakery workers forced bakery owners to hire foreign replacements, including skilled bakers from Austria.

title: Maple Pumpkin Spice Latte Syrup
description: Fall flavours 03: maple pumpkin spice latte.

ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup brown sugar (adjust depending on desired sweetness)

steps: Combine all ingredients over high heat, then lower to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Let cool, remove cinnamon sticks and pour into syrup bottle or jar.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Around fall the pumpkin spice latte explodes in the USA.

title: Saltah (Yemeni Beef Stew)
description: Is this the best dish in the world?
steps: The night before: soak the fenugreek seeds in hot water to take the bitterness out.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Brown the beef, then set aside.
Sauté the onions with a pinch of salt.
Add tomatoes, black pepper and turmeric.
Return the beef, pour in the stock and scrape the bottom of the pot.
Cover and cook 45 min, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, grind everything for the zhug in a mortar and pestle.
Drain the fenugreek, grind it in the mortar and pestle, add fresh cold water and let it soak.
Add potatoes to the stew, cook another 25 min (or till fork tender).
Drain excess water off the fenugreek, then whip with cold water till foamy.
Stir chopped herbs, beaten eggs and some zhug through the stew.
Serve with fenugreek foam and extra zhug on top.

cultural relevance.reasoning: This is Yemen's national dish.

title: Poutine
description: Do you agree with my rating?
steps: Wash the potatoes and cut into fries, skin on. Pat completely dry.
Fry at 175°C (350°F) for 5-7 min until just lightly colored around the edges. Drain and set aside.
For the gravy, mix the garlic powder, onion powder, soy sauce, Worcestershire and stock so it's ready to go.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until bubbling.
Add the flour and whisk for 1 min until light blonde.
Slowly pour in the stock mix while whisking, season with salt & pepper and simmer until thick.
Fry the potatoes again at 205°C (400°F) until golden brown.
Toss in a big bowl with salt.
Plate with the cheese curds and pour the hot gravy over the top.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Québécois comfort food made of french fries and fresh cheese curds topped with hot brown gravy, originating in rural Quebec in the late 1950s and growing into a major symbol of Québécois and Canadian food culture.

title: Kimchi Jjigae
description: How is something so simple yet so good?

ingredients.raw: Gochugaru 2 tbsp (use half if you don't like spicy) (sauce mix)

steps: Mix the sauce ingredients together.
Finely dice the garlic, cut pork belly into bite size pieces.
Sauté pork belly with garlic.
Add kimchi and sauce mix, stir fry a few more minutes.
Add water and hondashi, simmer for 20 minutes (1 hour is even better).
Taste the soup: add water if too salty, reduce further if too weak.
Add tofu, cook 5 more minutes.
Finish with spring onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.
Serve with rice.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Traditional Korean stew made primarily with aged kimchi, meat or seafood, tofu, and broth.

title: Tarte Tatin
description: It's a classic for a reason because there's not many people on this planet that don't like it. This is my Tarte Tatin, which is classically an apple Tarte Tatin.

ingredients.raw: 4-5 Apples, peeled, sliced thinly and dried on some paper towels for 10 mins or so
Ice Cream and Walnuts to serve
Ice Cream and Walnuts to serve

steps: In a cold pan, press your butter down covering the bottom of the pan.
Sprinkle your sugar on top of the butter along with your cinnamon.
Add your star anise to the centre of the pan.
Lay your apple disks around the pan in a neat formation until you have a few layers.
Turn the heat to medium low and wait 10 minutes or so for the caramel to form and bubble up the sides of the apples.
Lay your puff pastry over the top, tuck the edges, prick with a fork and make a hole in the centre.
Get it in the oven at 180°C for 40-45 minutes.
Remove from the oven, flip out onto a plate and top with your ice cream and walnuts. Enjoy!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Classic French upside-down tart made by caramelizing fruit, typically apples, in butter ans sugar.

title: Potato & Leek Soup

ingredients.raw: 1 small bunch kale, stems removed and leaves torn

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the leek and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the carrots, garlic, smoked paprika, thyme and oregano. Cook for another 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the potatoes, butter beans and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for around 10 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Blend half the soup just by using a stick blender directly in the pot until happy with the texture.
Stir in the coconut milk and kale. Cover and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the kale is tender but still bright green.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Serve with grated Parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil and fresh baguette.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Classic, hearty dish made primarily from leeks and potatoes simmered in broth, prized for its comforting simplicity.

title: Quesillo
description: Forever favorites. What do you call this? You'll say, "But you're fit, how do you eat this?" Well, yes, I do, because there's nothing wrong with enjoying what you like and what makes you happy in a healthy way.
steps: Caramel: cook the sugar and water over low heat until all the sugar dissolves and the caramel forms. Be careful not to burn yourself.
Mixture: put everything in the blender and blend for 1 minute straight.
Pour it into the mold once the caramel has cooled.
Cover and cook in a water bath (bain-marie) for 45-50 minutes.
Remove carefully and refrigerate for at least 5 hours.
Then enjoy with everyone at home!

cultural relevance.reasoning: Famous artesanal string cheese in Mexico.

title: Pasta with Shrimp and Olive Chimichurri
description: This is the perfect recipe to make on the weekend: easy, delicious and ready in 20 minutes!!! The secret of this recipe is the quality of the oil.

ingredients.raw: 6 tbsp Mesa Sana ultra premium extra virgin olive oil
1 cup Parmesan cheese, grated with a microplane, extra to serve
1/2 cup chopped parsley, extra to serve
2 cans green olives, drained and chopped

steps: In a pot with plenty of boiling salted water, cook the pasta according to the package instructions. Set aside 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
In a hot pan, add a little oil and sauté the garlic. Cook the shrimp 1 to 2 minutes per side (don't overcook them) and set them aside.

In the same pan, add more oil, the garlic and the peperoncino and cook for a few seconds until fragrant. Add the white wine and let it reduce by half. Add the butter, some of the Parmesan and the lime juice, and mix.
Add the parsley, the olives, the shrimp and the pasta and mix well with the sauce. Taste and adjust the seasoning, and add a little of the pasta water if it feels too thick.
Serve sprinkled with more parsley, Parmesan and lemon zest.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Chimichurri is a tangy, herb-based sauce from Argentina and Uruguay that originated from European migration to the Rio de la Plata region.

title: Salmon Bowl with Spicy Yogurt Sauce
description: Flavorful and satisfying. The caramelized salmon, fresh crunchy veggies, pickled onions, rice, and that creamy spicy yogurt sauce all together.

ingredients.raw: Chopped cucumber + fresh parsley + fresh lemon juice (cucumber salad)
Chopped cucumber + fresh parsley + fresh lemon juice (cucumber salad)
Chopped cucumber + fresh parsley + fresh lemon juice (cucumber salad)
Thinly sliced red onion + apple cider vinegar + pinch of salt + drizzle of honey + black pepper (quick pickled onions)
Thinly sliced red onion + apple cider vinegar + pinch of salt + drizzle of honey + black pepper (quick pickled onions)
Thinly sliced red onion + apple cider vinegar + pinch of salt + drizzle of honey + black pepper (quick pickled onions)
Thinly sliced red onion + apple cider vinegar + pinch of salt + drizzle of honey + black pepper (quick pickled onions)
Thinly sliced red onion + apple cider vinegar + pinch of salt + drizzle of honey + black pepper (quick pickled onions)
Rice • salmon • shredded carrots • cucumber salad • pickled onions • spicy yogurt sauce (to build your bowl)
Rice • salmon • shredded carrots • cucumber salad • pickled onions • spicy yogurt sauce (to build your bowl)

steps: Salmon: Toss everything together and arrange the salmon in a single layer in your air fryer basket or on a baking sheet. Broil for about 8-10 minutes, until cooked through and lightly caramelized.
Spicy yogurt sauce: Whisk until smooth. Adjust the sriracha and honey depending on how spicy or sweet you like it.
Cucumber salad: Mix the chopped cucumber, fresh parsley and fresh lemon juice.
Quick pickled onions: Combine the thinly sliced red onion, apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, a drizzle of honey and black pepper. Let sit for 15-20 minutes.
To build your bowl: Rice, salmon, shredded carrots, cucumber salad, pickled onions and spicy yogurt sauce.

title: Brownie, Lucuma and Manjar Copón (Trifle Cup)
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
In a pot, melt the chocolate together with the butter and the coffee and let it cool down. In a bowl, mix the eggs with the sugars.
Add the flour with the cocoa, and finally fold in the chocolate and butter mixture. Pour into a square pan lined with parchment paper and bake for about 25 minutes.
Whip the well-chilled cream and fold in the lucuma purée. Finally, cut the brownies into small squares.
To assemble the copón, place a layer of brownies at the base, then a layer of manjar, lucuma cream and chopped walnuts. Finish with lucuma cream and refrigerate.
Before serving, decorate with pieces of brownie, some walnuts and, optionally, more manjar.

cultural relevance.reasoning: South American fusion dessert that layes native Andean ingredients with colonial dairy traditions and North American baking.

title: Kaiserschmarrn with Zwetschkenröster and Apfelmus
description: The 'schmarrn' (mess) part of the name relates to the fact that it's, you know, bashed about and messed up.
steps: Rum raisins - Combine raisins and rum a couple of hours ahead (or the night before). Refrigerate.

Zwetschkenröster - Wash, halve and de-stone the plums. Add to a pan with everything else except rum. Cook gently until plums soften and syrup turns nicely purple. Add rum and optionally 10g caramelised sugar. It should be thick, with plums just holding their shape. Cool and refrigerate.
Apfelmus - Peel and dice apples. Add to a pan with the remaining ingredients and a dash of water to get going. Cook until almost completely broken down, then sieve. Cool and refrigerate.

Batter - Separate egg whites and yolks in different bowls. Whisk vanilla extract, whole milk, flour (I add it in parts) and a pinch of salt into yolks. Whisk whites with 40g sugar to soft peaks, then carefully fold into batter.

Melt 30g butter in a frying pan over medium, spread and add the batter. Sprinkle over rum raisins. Check sides occasionally with a spatula for browning; the bottom will be darker. Once sides are light brown, cut into large pieces and flip. Wait a few minutes for more browning, flip again, then as the whole mixture is almost set, rip it open and bash it about with a spatula. Once fully cooked, push aside. Add 20g butter and 25g sugar to the cleared space. Melt, stir, then toss Kaiserschmarrn through and caramelise edges for a couple of minutes.
Plate up, dust with icing sugar and serve with fruit compotes.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Shredded pancake rooted in the 19th-century Habsburg Empire.

title: 3-Ingredient Thanksgiving Gravy

ingredients.raw: 6 cups turkey or chicken stock, preferably homemade
1/3 cup rendered turkey fat or olive oil
Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper

steps: Bring stock to a boil in a medium pot; continue to boil until reduced slightly, about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook flour and fat in a large skillet over medium heat, whisking constantly, until roux has a coppery brown hue, about 5 minutes. Whisk in wine and bring to a boil; cook, whisking constantly, until mixture no longer smells like alcohol, about 2 minutes. Gradually ladle in hot stock, whisking after each addition. Continue to boil, whisking occasionally, until gravy coats the back of a spoon, 20–25 minutes (if gravy gets too thick, whisk in a bit of water or pan juices until it reaches the desired consistency). Season to taste with salt and pepper.

Do ahead: Gravy can be made 3 days ahead; transfer to an airtight container and chill. Heat in a small pot over medium, whisking constantly and adding warm water or pan juices 1 Tbsp. at a time if needed, until smooth.

Cooks' note: To utilize turkey fat and pan juices in this recipe, pour the pan drippings through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup, then skim off the fat and transfer to a small bowl. (If using a fat separator, pour pan drippings through sieve into separator and let stand until fat rises to top, 1–2 minutes.) Use the fat as the base for your roux. For a deeper, richer flavor, add some pan juices from roasting your turkey to the gravy as you finish it. You can also use the pan juices to thin out an already-prepared gravy when you reheat it.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Thanksgiving item.

title: Chicken Fajitas

ingredients.raw: 1 bunch cilantro, plus sprigs for serving
6 Tbsp. (or more) extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 Tbsp. plus 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 2 tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided, plus more
1 1/4 tsp. freshly ground pepper, divided, plus more
3 lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs or breasts
4 medium red, yellow, orange, and/or green bell peppers, ribs and stems removed, cut into 1/2"-thick strips
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)
Warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, and lime wedges (for serving)

steps: Peel and quarter 1 large onion and transfer to a blender. Add 1 bunch cilantro, zest and juice of 2 oranges, zest and juice of 3 limes, 6 garlic cloves, peeled, 4 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 2 Tbsp. ancho chile powder, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 3/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt, 2 tsp. ground cumin, 1 tsp. dried Mexican oregano, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, 1 tsp. ground coriander, and 1 tsp. smoked paprika and blend marinade until smooth.

Place 3 lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs or breasts in a medium bowl. Pour marinade over and toss to coat. Let sit at room temperature at least 30 minutes or cover and chill up to 4 hours. If chilling, let sit at room temperature 30 minutes before cooking.

Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess drip back into bowl, and place on a large plate; discard marinade. Pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with a big pinch of salt. Heat remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Working in batches and adding more oil between batches if pan looks dry, cook chicken in a single layer, undisturbed, until deep golden brown, about 5 minutes. Turn over and cook, on other side until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part registers 165° (or 160° if using chicken breasts), 5–7 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Wipe out skillet and reserve.

Halve remaining 2 large onions through root end. Peel and slice 1/2" thick. Add more oil to reserved skillet if needed and cook onions and 4 medium red, yellow, orange, and/or green bell peppers, ribs and stems removed, cut into 1/2"-thick strips, undisturbed, 2 minutes. Sprinkle in 1/2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1/4 tsp. Morton kosher salt and 1/4 tsp. freshly ground pepper and stir to combine. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally and adding 1 Tbsp. water at a time if vegetables are beginning to stick to bottom of pan to loosen brown bits (let water absorb completely before adding more), until vegetables are browned around the edges and softened, 8–12 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Taste onion mixture and season with more salt and pepper if needed.

Remove foil from chicken and slice into 1/2"-thick strips. Return to skillet; toss to combine. Serve with warm corn tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, coarsely grated Monterey Jack, pico de gallo, cilantro sprigs, and lime wedges for making fajitas.

cultural relevance.reasoning: It is a culFajitas originated in the 1930s in South Texas.

title: Chicken Salad with Crème Fraîche and Rye

ingredients.raw: 1 large skin-on, bone-in chicken breast (12-14 ounces)
3/4 cup fresh fava beans (from about 3/4 pound pods) or frozen, thawed
1/2 small English hothouse cucumber, very thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
8 slices Danish rye bread or other dense health bread, toasted if desired

steps: Preheat oven to 425°. Place chicken on a small rimmed baking sheet and rub with 1 tablespoon oil; season with kosher salt and pepper. Roast until golden brown and cooked through, 25-30 minutes. Let cool, then shred into bite-size pieces.

If using fresh fava beans, cook in a large saucepan of boiling salted water until tender, about 4 minutes. Drain and transfer to a bowl of ice water. Drain and peel. (If using frozen fava beans, cook 2 minutes; transfer to a bowl of ice water, then drain.) Toss in a large bowl with fennel, scallion, tarragon, vinegar, chicken, and remaining 3 tablespoons oil; season with kosher salt, pepper, and more vinegar, if desired.
Meanwhile, whisk crème fraîche in a medium bowl to soft peaks (it will look fluffy); season with kosher salt.
Toss cucumber with parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a small bowl; season with kosher salt and pepper.
Serve chicken salad with bread, cucumber, and a dollop of crème fraîche, topped with sea salt and more pepper.
Do ahead: Chicken can be cooked 2 days ahead; cover and chill. Shred just before using. Fava beans can be cooked 2 days ahead; cover and chill.

title: Chickpea Salad With Lemon, Parmesan, and Fresh Herbs
steps: Combine rinsed and drained chickpeas, chopped fresh basil, chopped Italian parsley, fresh lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, and pressed garlic clove in medium bowl. Add grated Parmesan cheese and toss gently to blend all ingredients thoroughly. Season chickpea salad to taste with coarse kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.
DO AHEAD: Chickpea salad can be made 4 hours ahead. Cover and refrigerate. Serve salad chilled or at room temperature.

title: Corn and Zucchini Salad with Feta

ingredients.raw: 4 small zucchini (about 1 1/2 pounds), thinly sliced lengthwise on a mandoline
8-10 zucchini blossoms, torn into large pieces (optional)
1/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley

steps: Cook corn in a large pot of boiling salted water until bright yellow and tender, about 3 minutes; transfer to a plate and let cool.

Cut kernels from cobs and place in a large bowl. Add zucchini, zucchini blossoms (if using), basil, parsley, oil, vinegar, and red pepper flakes and toss to combine; season with salt and pepper. Serve topped with feta.
Do ahead: Corn can be cooked 1 day ahead. Cut kernels from cobs; cover and chill. Bring to room temperature before using.

title: Eggplant With Lentils and Goat Cheese

ingredients.raw: 2 globe eggplants (1 pound each), halved lengthwise
2 cups packaged steamed lentils (such as Melissa's)
1/4 cup chopped fresh mint, plus torn leaves for serving

steps: Heat oven to 475°. Remove pulp from eggplants; cut pulp from one eggplant into 1/4-inch cubes and discard the rest. Coat eggplant shells with cooking spray; sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon salt. On a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, place eggplant shells open side down. In a bowl, coat eggplant cubes with cooking spray and toss with 1/4 teaspoon salt; place in one layer on a second baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake eggplant shells and cubes until tender, 10 minutes. Remove eggplant; reduce oven to 350°. In a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat, heat oil. Cook onion, celery and carrot until soft, 5 minutes. Add garlic; cook, 1 minute. Add lentils, eggplant cubes, broth, vinegar, pepper and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt; reduce heat to simmer, stirring occasionally, 5 minutes. Stir in chopped mint. Flip shells on baking sheet and stuff with lentil-eggplant mixture; cover with aluminum foil and bake until warm; 10 minutes. Top with cheese and mint leaves.

title: Green Mango Salad

ingredients.raw: 2 Thai green or red chiles, with seeds, chopped
2 teaspoons palm or light brown sugar
4 green mangoes or 1 green papaya, julienned on a mandoline
1/2 cup unsalted, dry-roasted peanuts, coarsely chopped

steps: Purée chiles, garlic, lime juice, fish sauce, oil, and palm sugar in a blender until smooth.
Toss mangoes, shallots, peanuts, cilantro, mint, dried shrimp, if using, sesame seeds, and dressing in a large bowl; season with salt.
DO AHEAD: Dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Cover and chill.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Known as Yam Mamuang in Thailand, it is a staple across Southeast Asia.

title: Grilled Lettuces with Crème Fraîche and Avocado

ingredients.raw: 2 romaine lettuce hearts and/or large heads of Treviso radicchio, halved lengthwise
3 tablespoons olive oil, divided, plus more
1 cup mizuna or baby mustard greens

steps: Prepare grill for medium-high heat. Brush cut sides of lettuce with a total of 2 tablespoons oil; season with kosher salt and pepper. Grill lettuce, cut side down, until lightly charred, about 2 minutes.
Toss mizuna with 1 tablespoon oil in a medium bowl; season with kosher salt.
Dollop crème fraîche on a platter and top with grilled lettuce and avocado; scatter mizuna over. Drizzle with lemon juice and more oil; season with sea salt and pepper.

title: Grilled Zucchini and Leeks with Walnuts and Herbs

ingredients.raw: 2 large leeks, white and pale-green parts only, halved lengthwise with some root attached
1/2 cup (lightly packed) fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves with tender stems

steps: Prepare grill for medium-high heat. Toast walnuts in a dry small skillet over medium heat, tossing often, until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Chop very coarsely. Toss warm walnuts with garlic, lemon juice, and 3 tablespoons oil in a large bowl; season with salt and pepper.

Brush leeks and zucchini with remaining 2 tablespoons oil; season with salt and pepper. Grill vegetables, turning often, until tender and charred in spots, 5-8 minutes for leeks, 8-10 minutes for zucchini.

Transfer vegetables to a cutting board. Trim roots from leeks and cut leeks and zucchini into bite-size pieces. Add vegetables and parsley to bowl with walnuts and toss to combine; season vegetables with salt, pepper, and more lemon juice, if desired.

title: Linguine with Burst Tomatoes and Chiles

ingredients.raw: 2 1/4"-thick slices crusty bread, well-toasted, broken into pieces
1 tablespoon chopped drained oil-packed Calabrian chiles

steps: Pulse toast in a food processor to fine crumbs; set aside.
Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente; drain, reserving 1 1/2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Meanwhile, heat chiles and 3 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat until sizzling, about 2 minutes. Add tomatoes, increase heat to medium-high, and cook, turning tomatoes occasionally, until blistered in spots, about 3 minutes. Continue to cook, lightly crushing tomatoes, until beginning to break down, about 3 minutes.
Add pasta, 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and 1/4 cup Pecorino to skillet and cook, tossing and adding more liquid as needed, until sauce coats pasta, about 2 minutes.
Serve pasta seasoned with salt and pepper and topped with remaining Pecorino and reserved breadcrumbs.

cultural relevance.reasoning: Inpired in italian flavors and ingredients.

title: Linguine with Green Olive Sauce and Zesty Breadcrumbs

ingredients.raw: 12 ounces linguine or other long pasta
1/2 ounce Parmesan, finely grated (about 1/2 cup), plus more for serving

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a medium skillet over medium and cook panko, stirring, until golden, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper; transfer to paper towels to drain and toss with dill and lemon zest.
Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente. Drain, reserving 1/2 cup pasta cooking liquid.

Meanwhile, mash anchovies and garlic to a paste on a cutting board with the side of a chef's knife. Combine with parsley, basil, and half of olives and capers in a large bowl. Chop remaining olives and capers and add to bowl, along with remaining 1/2 cup oil. Mix well; season sauce with salt and pepper.

Add pasta and 1/4 cup reserved pasta cooking liquid to sauce. Toss, adding Parmesan a bit at a time, along with more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until sauce coats pasta. Add lemon juice; season with salt and pepper.
Serve pasta topped with panko and more Parmesan.
Do ahead: Sauce can be made 1 day ahead. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly against surface, and chill.

cultural relevance.reasoning: This recipe has mediterranean flavors (olives, capers, anchovies, etc.) and uses mollica atturrata ("poor man's parmesan"), the breadcrumbs.

title: Mussels in Lager

ingredients.raw: 2 celery ribs, cut into 1/4-inch dice (1 cup)
1 cup drained canned diced tomatoes (from a 14- to 15-oz can)
2 cups lager such as Harp (16 oz; pour beer slowly into measuring cup; do not measure foam)
2 lb mussels (preferably cultivated), scrubbed well and beards removed

steps: Heat butter in a wide 5- to 6-quart heavy pot over moderately high heat until foam subsides, then cook onion, celery, tomatoes, garlic, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are softened, about 4 minutes.

Add beer and bring just to a boil. Add mussels and cook, covered, stirring occasionally, until mussels open wide, 4 to 6 minutes, transferring them to a bowl as they open. (Discard any mussels that remain unopened after 6 minutes.) Remove pot from heat. Stir together mustard and cream in a small bowl, then add mixture along with parsley to hot broth and whisk until combined. Discard bay leaf. Serve sauce over mussels.

cultural relevance.reasoning: In Belgium, mussels are typically steamed in beer (Belgian ale) instead of wine.

title: No-Churn Ginger-Vanilla Fro Yo With Peach Compote

ingredients.raw: 3 cups (or 6 store-bought cups, 4 ounces each) lowfat vanilla pudding
1/4 cup (1 ounce) crystallized ginger, finely chopped
2 large (1 1/4 pounds) ripe peaches, pitted and sliced, slices halved (or 10 oz frozen peach slices, thawed )
1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, plus more for garnish

steps: In a bowl, whisk together yogurt, pudding, crystallized ginger, honey and vanilla until smooth. Freeze until solid, 4 to 6 hours. Remove from freezer and defrost slightly, 15 minutes. In a medium saucepan, bring to a low boil peaches, 1 tablespoon water, sugar, fresh ginger and cinnamon; reduce heat and simmer until liquid thickens and peaches soften slightly, 4 to 5 minutes. Remove from heat; let cool. In a food processor, process frozen yogurt-pudding mixture until smooth. Divide fro yo and peach compote among 6 bowls; sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Perfect Fish Tacos
description: Special equipment: A deep-fry thermometer

ingredients.raw: 2 pounds skinless red snapper or other mild white fish fillets (fish)
Fresno Chile Hot Sauce, for serving (assembly)
Sliced avocado, cilantro leaves with tender stems, Sliced pickled jalapeños, and lime wedges for serving (assembly)
Sliced avocado, cilantro leaves with tender stems, Sliced pickled jalapeños, and lime wedges for serving (assembly)
Sliced avocado, cilantro leaves with tender stems, Sliced pickled jalapeños, and lime wedges for serving (assembly)
Sliced avocado, cilantro leaves with tender stems, Sliced pickled jalapeños, and lime wedges for serving (assembly)

steps: Prepare and Cut Fish: Remove any pin bones from fish fillets (using tweezers makes this easy). Cut each fillet in half lengthwise. Cut each half on a diagonal into 1" strips. (Work with the natural shape of the fish as you cut; this will help the pieces stay together instead of falling apart when frying.)

Make Batter: Whisk all-purpose flour, rice flour, and salt in a medium bowl. Gradually whisk in club soda until no lumps remain; adjust with more club soda or rice flour as needed to make it the consistency of thin pancake batter—it should be pourable, but thick enough to coat the fish.
Heat Oil: Fit a large pot with a deep-fry thermometer and pour in oil to measure 2". Heat over medium-high heat until thermometer registers 350°.

Batter and Fry Fish: Working in batches of 5–7 pieces at a time, coat fish in batter, letting excess drip off, then carefully place in oil (to avoid splattering, lower fish into oil pointing away from you). Don’t overcrowd the pot: The oil temperature will drop dramatically and fish may stick together.
Fry fish, turning occasionally with a fish spatula or slotted spoon and maintaining oil temperature at 350°, until crust is puffed, crisp, and golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Transfer to a wire rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet; season immediately with salt.
Warm Tortillas: While fish is frying, use tongs to heat tortillas one at a time directly over a gas burner, moving them often, until lightly charred and puffed in spots, about 1 minute per side.
Transfer to a plate; cover with a clean kitchen towel to keep warm. (If you don’t have a gas stove, wrap up a stack of tortillas in a sheet of foil and heat in a 350° oven until warmed through.)
Serve: Top tortillas (we like two per taco) with fish, slaw, hot sauce, avocado, cilantro, and pickled jalapeños. Serve with lime wedges.

cultural relevance.reasoning: From the Ensenada, Baja California region in Mexico. Fish tacos have become an iconic Mexican dish.

title: Pork Tenderloin with Date and Cilantro Relish

ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup Medjool dates (about 4 ounces), cut into small pieces
3 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro plus leaves for serving

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Season pork with salt and pepper and cook, turning, until browned on all sides, 6–8 minutes. Transfer skillet to oven and cook pork until an instant-read thermometer inserted in thickest part registers 140°F, 10–15 minutes. Transfer pork to a cutting board and let rest at least 5 minutes before slicing; set aside pan drippings.

Toss dates, orange juice, reserved pan drippings, 3 tablespoons chopped cilantro, and remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a small bowl; season with salt and pepper. Spoon relish over pork and top with cilantro leaves.
DO AHEAD: Relish (without pan drippings) can be made 4 hours ahead. Cover and chill. Add pan drippings just before serving.

title: Simple Classic Stuffing

ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, plus more for baking dish
1 lb. good-quality day-old white bread, torn into 1" pieces (about 10 cups)
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth, divided

steps: Preheat oven to 250°. Grease a 13x9x2" baking dish with unsalted butter and set aside. Scatter 1 lb. good-quality day-old white bread, torn into 1" pieces (about 10 cups), in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake, stirring occasionally, until dried out, about 1 hour. Let cool; transfer to a very large bowl.

Meanwhile, melt 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat; add 2 1/2 cups chopped yellow onions and 1 1/2 cups (1/4" slices) celery to melted butter. Stir often until just beginning to brown, about 10 minutes. Add to bowl with dried bread cubes; stir in 1/2 cup chopped flat-leaf parsley, 2 Tbsp. chopped fresh sage, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh rosemary, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh thyme, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. freshly ground black pepper. Drizzle in 1 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth and toss gently. Let cool.
